title: P0 BUG — cache-replay persist_artifacts emit raises AttributeError, swallowed by bare except
description:
At tests/benchmark_harness.py:215-219, the cache-replay synthesizer for persist_artifacts does `(cached.clusters or {}).values()` but `cached.clusters` is `list[dict]` (per CachedNerResult at libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/cluster_cache.py:72). The .values() call raises AttributeError; a bare `except: pass` upstream swallows it; result: ZERO persist_artifacts events emitted on warm replay paths. Discovered by Gap #10 critic+DS verifier (review at .test-output/inspector-tour/qa-verify/gap-10-review.md).

Fix: change `(cached.clusters or {}).values()` → iterate the list directly. Drop the bare except so future bugs don't hide. Add a regression test that exercises the cache-replay branch end-to-end and asserts a persist_artifacts event lands in the audit log.

Sibling: CD-niob (cold-path emit), CD-1qqy (e2e fixture corpus — would have caught this immediately).
close_reason: landed in 9a24ffc — list iteration + dict.get for propositions; bare except narrowed to logger.exception(); regression test in tests/test_replay_phase_a_persist_artifacts.py passing

title: P0 Add source_code_locations column to canonical_entities Postgres schema
description: canonical_entities.py:148 writes source_code_locations (sorted list of code_location names per canonical entity) but GraphDBResource.upsert_canonical_entities silently drops it because the Postgres schema has no such column. Add a migration creating the column as TEXT[] with a default of '{}', update the upsert SQL to include it, and extend the CanonicalEntity ORM/dataclass round-trip test to assert the column survives. Without this, downstream provenance queries ('which source produced this canonical') are broken. This is a prerequisite for the Path C fix landing cleanly and for the new dashboard 'Entity Concordance — Convergence' row to show source coverage.

CD-7np: source_code_locations TEXT[] column + 3-layer migration (ConfigMap + runtime ALTER) + 8 schema tests passing. title: P0 Path C: eliminate silent path_builder fallback, require explicit code_location
description: Durable fix for the silent-zero path-resolution bug behind CD-pzc. path_builder.py:52-68 currently tries a deprecated Dagster API (context.step_context.dagster_run.external_pipeline_origin.external_repository_origin.code_location_origin.location_name) and on any failure silently falls back to os.environ.get('DAGSTER_CODE_LOCATION', 'default') — this silent fallback is exactly what caused the media_ingest to default path divergence. Fix: (1) introduce a CodeLocationResource (Pydantic ConfigurableResource) that takes a required code_location: str field at definition time, (2) thread the resource into MinioIOManager + OptionalMinioIOManager so build_asset_root reads from the resource instead of introspecting context, (3) delete the env-var fallback and the deprecated API call — on inability to determine code_location, raise a DagsterInvalidConfigError at startup, not at runtime. (4) Update each code location's Definitions (congress_data, open_leaks, media_ingest, knowledge_graph) to pass its own code_location string. (5) Rebuild dagster-io wheel and redeploy all 4 code locations. Requires Path A already in place (don't break prod twice). Depends on schema migration CD-<canonical_cols> landing in parallel.
acceptance_criteria: path_builder.py has no env-var fallback and no deprecated external_pipeline_origin access, CodeLocationResource is required in every code location's Definitions, unit test exercises build_asset_root under both OutputContext and InputContext with an explicit resource and asserts paths match {layer}/{code_location}/{group}/{asset}, all 4 code locations deploy and materialize at least one test asset end-to-end, no silent defaults possible (grep for DAGSTER_CODE_LOCATION in dagster-io returns zero hits).
close_reason: Path C work shipped in commit b788562 and verified end-to-end by run 3f58561a. Blocker CD-7np (source_code_locations schema column) is separate completeness work, not a prerequisite — the P0 fix is verified to work without it.

title: P0 Path A: S3 migrate gold/default/media and set DAGSTER_CODE_LOCATION
description: EMERGENCY STOP for the canonical_entities silent-zero bug. Producer writes to s3://dagster/gold/default/media/* but consumer expects s3://dagster/gold/media_ingest/media/* because path_builder.py:64-68 silently falls back to os.environ.get('DAGSTER_CODE_LOCATION', 'default') and the media-ingest deployment has no such env var set. This task is the immediate unblock: (1) aws s3 mv (or rclone) the existing default/media/* tree under gold/ to media_ingest/media/* preserving all partition paths and _metadata.json sidecars, (2) set DAGSTER_CODE_LOCATION=media_ingest as an env var on the media-ingest Deployment in k8s/media-ingest/deployment.yaml, (3) redeploy and re-run canonical_entities to verify non-zero writes. A separate subagent is executing this NOW so the task is created in_progress and claimed to avoid conflicts with the proper fix (Path C). This is the band-aid; Path C is the durable fix.

title: Decouple e2e test fixture corpus from dev/latest bench runs
description:
Today every Playwright spec under packages/media-ingest/viewer-ui/e2e/ resolves a target run via /viewer/api/bench/runs?latest. That endpoint returns whatever bench the developer most recently ran — fixture data is non-deterministic and frequently missing the shapes specs need. Just ran a 12.8min e2e suite (Gap #1-#4) and got 17 pass / 15 skip / 2 fail; **13 of the 15 skips were direct dev-data limitations**, not test bugs.

## Specific fixture gaps observed

- Active GT (s3://dagster/bench/ground-truth/active.json) has 0 populated mentions → 8+ tests skip (Gap #1 F1 strip rendering, GT-confirmed chip on accepted/rejected, Gap #3 confidence-histogram GT overlay)
- Latest run uses only 2 encoders (testing1 pipeline) → 4+ Gap #2 matrix tests skip (need ≥3-encoder doc for matrix-render, lone-voter-diagonal, click-to-filter, mode-toggle-produces-different-Jaccards)
- No mention_rejected events with source_models field → Gap #9 lone-voter-chip / multi-encoder-chip / Gap-#2-cross-cut tests skip (predates the Gap #9 backend emit)
- No SPO events with prompt_hash field → Gap #5 prompt-pane / response-pane / parse-errors tests skip (pre-Gap-#5 backend)
- No persist_artifacts events outside cache-replay → Gap #10 panel-renders / per-asset-card / dagster-deep-link / partial-failure tests skip (cold-path persist op doesn't yet call emit_persist_artifacts — see CD-niob's sibling backlog)
- No legacy chars_per_mention=null records → Gap #4 legacy-record test skips
- No composite-reason pruned windows (both too_few_mentions AND sparse_density) → Gap #7 follow-up composite test skips
- No encoder with uniformly null confidence → Gap #3 empty-state test skips

## Proposed approach (layered)

**Layer 1: snapshotted real runs** — pick 3-4 dev runs that together cover the shape matrix; freeze their event NDJSON + report.json + active-gt.json under packages/media-ingest/viewer-ui/e2e/fixtures/snapshots/. Each ~1-5MB, JSONL, git-friendly. Fixture #1: full 4-encoder run with populated GT + persist + SPO. Fixture #2: 3-encoder run with composite-reason pruning. Fixture #3: partial-failure persist run.

**Layer 2: synthetic edge-case seeder** — for shapes that don't naturally occur (legacy null cpm, composite reasons, multi-error parse_errors), a deterministic Python script that synthesizes the events directly into a sandboxed event_store. Run as a pre-test hook.

**Layer 3: pre-test injection** — Playwright globalSetup mounts the snapshots+synthetic events into a dedicated bench/test-fixtures/ S3 prefix (or serves them via a mock route). The discovery helpers (e2e/fixtures/inspector-discovery.ts) point at that prefix via a new TEST_FIXTURE_RUN_ID env var. Specs never see /viewer/api/bench/runs?latest in test mode.

**Acceptance criteria**:
- Re-running the e2e suite N times yields deterministic pass/skip counts (today: variable)
- All 13 currently-skipping tests due to data shape now satisfy their preconditions
- CI doesn't require a live bench — just the viewer-ui dev server + fixture corpus
- A regen script (mise exec -- python scripts/dev/snapshot_e2e_fixtures.py) rebuilds the snapshots from current dev when the test corpus drifts intentionally
- Dev workflow: developer can still run /viewer/benchmarks/state against their live bench; fixture isolation is opt-in via PLAYWRIGHT_FIXTURE_MODE=on

## Out of scope
- Implementing the cold-path persist emit (CD-niob backlog)
- Backfilling source_models on historical events (Gap #9 emit-only-going-forward)
notes: Phase 1.5 partial — happy-path + trend-window corpora landed in 4812be7. Stub manifests for diversity-composite + edge-cases. See commit message for 4 follow-up TODOs (full corpora, wire useFixtureCorpus into specs 2/3/4/7/8/9/10, drop test.skip guards, task wrapper).
close_reason: all 4 corpora landed, 7 gap specs wired, task test:e2e:fixtures shipped

title: gliner-large emitting 25k+ mentions vs ≤63 from peer encoders (huge dedup/threshold regression)
description:
Latest full-corpus bench (run 2026-05-04-185418, 33.8min wall): gliner-large produced 25,109 mentions while every other encoder produced ≤63 on the same corpus. This is a 400× anomaly vs prior smoke runs (the same model produced ~7 mentions on hr5376-117 in the smaller-sample bench).

Smoking gun candidates (in priority order):
1. Recent commit 73ea4df (gliner-pii taxonomy expand) or 4e1db24 (PII-only label restriction) accidentally affected gliner-large too — the GLiNERClient label-set logic in gliner.py:_extract_mentions branches on `'pii' in self.model_name.lower()` but maybe the model_name resolution is now wrong.
2. The PII_GLINER_LABELS branch isn't being taken for gliner-pii anymore so it falls back to the full label set + something is also dropping the dedup-by-(start,end,label).
3. GLINER_THRESHOLD env var got reset / unset, threshold=0 means everything.
4. Window overlap dedup broken: gliner.py has a (start, end, label) seen-set at line ~165 — if windows are running 10× as many overlapping windows after a recent change, dedup might be not catching them.

Repro: clone fresh, run `task bench:run -- --ensemble gliner-medium,gliner-large,gliner-pii,nuextract-2.0-8b,universalner-7b --spo-models llama3.1-8b --sample-per-domain 1`. Compare mention counts vs the smoke baseline in 2026-05-03-185305.

Diagnostic command:
  mise exec -- python -c "
  from dagster_io.bench import S3BenchmarkStore
  s = S3BenchmarkStore()
  ext = s.client.get_object('bench/runs/2026-05-04-185418/extractions/extraction_gliner-large.json')
  import json; d = json.loads(ext)
  m = d.get('mentions', [])
  print('total:', len(m))
  print('first 5:', [(x.get('text'), x.get('mention_type'), x.get('span_start'), x.get('span_end'), x.get('confidence')) for x in m[:5]])
  print('span dups:', len(m) - len(set((x.get('span_start'), x.get('span_end'), x.get('text')) for x in m)))
  "

Acceptance: gliner-large produces O(100s)–O(1000s) of mentions per full corpus, comparable to gliner-medium/gliner-pii. A regression test in libs/catalyst-langgraph-aio/tests/test_gliner_dedup.py asserts len(mentions) is bounded by len(set(spans)) for any test text.

title: v4 polish: bench-table per-encoder stats backfill + State Inspector chunk_extracted emits
description:
Two related polish issues exposed by the first v4 smoke run (commit 9c3c854).

**1. Bench table per-encoder stats are zeros** — the per-encoder + ensemble rows in the bench output show `Time=0.0s · Tok/s=0 · Calls=0 · Retry=0` because the encoder fixtures saved during Phase A only stamp `mention_count` + `assertion_count=0`. Wall clock + throughput data are already in the `ner_encoder_completed.details.duration_s` events that the harness emits, but they're not read back when building the fixture's `stats` dict.

**2. State Inspector cards are visually identical + OUTPUT pane shows 0 mentions** — the inspector renders one card per chunk_id encountered, but for v4-shaped chunk_ids (`{doc}:_ner_{encoder}`, `{doc}:_consensus`, `{doc}:{window_id}`), the cards show identical preview text and empty output panels because:
- Per-encoder `extract_ner` emits `chunk_loaded` with the same full doc text, no per-encoder mention list
- `chunk_extracted` events are NEVER emitted for `_ner_*` or `_consensus` chunk_ids in v4 (the legacy `emit_chunk_extracted_for_state` only ran in `build_ner_pipeline`, not `build_ensemble_pipeline`)
- Cards don't visually differentiate kind (encoder vs consensus vs window)

**Files:**
- `tests/benchmark_harness.py::_phase_a_build_cluster_cache` — read `ner_encoder_completed` event details and stamp duration_s + chunk_count + tokens_per_sec into per-encoder fixtures + the ensemble fixture
- `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/nodes/ner_ensemble.py` — emit `chunk_extracted` per (doc, encoder) at end of `_run_one`, with that encoder's mentions
- `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/nodes/consensus.py::ConsensusNode.__call__` — emit `chunk_loaded` (source text + summary) AND `chunk_extracted` (consensus mentions) for chunk_id `{doc}:_consensus`
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/extraction.py::_process_doc` SPO loop — verify per-window `chunk_extracted` fires; if not, add it
- `packages/media-ingest/viewer-ui/src/components/state/ChunkRail.tsx` — small visual differentiation: badge on cards by chunk_id pattern (NER · CONSENSUS · WIN-N)</description>
<design>**Bench table fix (Phase A backfill):**

In `_phase_a_build_cluster_cache`, after the ensemble pipeline returns, the harness has access to the audit events emitted during Phase A. Read those audit events back from the event_tail before saving fixtures:

```python
def _aggregate_encoder_stats(events: list[dict], encoder_name: str) -> dict:
    """Pull duration_s + per-doc count from ner_encoder_completed events."""
    matching = [e for e in events
                if e.get('node_name') == 'ner_encoder_completed'
                and e.get('model') == encoder_name]
    return {
        'duration_s': sum(e.get('details', {}).get('duration_s', 0.0) for e in matching),
        'chunk_count': len(matching),
        'mention_count': sum(e.get('details', {}).get('mention_count', 0) for e in matching),
    }
```

Stamp into each per-encoder fixture's `stats` dict:
```python
fixture['stats'] = {
    'mention_count': per_doc_mention_count,
    'assertion_count': 0,
    'duration_s': aggregated_duration,
    'tokens_per_sec': total_chars / 4 / aggregated_duration if aggregated_duration > 0 else 0,
    'llm_call_count': len(docs),  # one NER call per doc
    'chunk_count': len(docs),
    'mention_retries': 0,
    'proposition_retries': 0,
    'errors': 0,
}
```

For the ensemble fixture, the duration is the wall-clock of the entire Phase A (max of all encoders since they ran in parallel + the consensus + cluster + pack steps).

**State Inspector emits:**

`NerEnsembleNode._run_one` after collecting `accepted` mentions, emit chunk_extracted:
```python
event_tail.emit_chunk_extracted(
    chunk_id_for_encoder,
    model=encoder_name,
    doc_id=doc_id,
    mentions=accepted,
    propositions=[],
)
```

`ConsensusNode.__call__` after building the accepted list:
```python
consensus_chunk_id = f"{doc_id}:_consensus"
# Synthetic chunk_loaded so the rail card has source text
event_tail.emit_chunk_text(
    consensus_chunk_id,
    state.get('raw_text', '')[:4096],
    doc_id=doc_id,
    domain=state.get('source_metadata', {}).get('domain'),
    chunk_metadata={'kind': 'consensus', 'n_encoders': self.n_encoders, 'quorum': self.default_quorum},
)
# chunk_extracted with the consensus mentions
event_tail.emit_chunk_extracted(
    consensus_chunk_id,
    model='ensemble',
    doc_id=doc_id,
    mentions=accepted,
    propositions=[],
)
```

Per-window verification: read `_process_doc` for whether `emit_chunk_extracted` fires per window. If not, add at the end of the SPO loop body with `chunk_id=window_chunk_id, model=bench_model, mentions=[], propositions=spo_accepted`.

**ChunkRail card differentiation:**

In `ChunkRail.tsx`, when rendering a card, detect chunk_id pattern:
- `:_ner_<name>` → small "NER" badge top-right, color encoded by tier
- `:_consensus` → "CONSENSUS" badge in cyan/magenta
- `:win-<id>` → "WIN-<short>" badge in default color
- Else → no badge (legacy chunks)

One-line conditional addition to the existing card render in ChunkRail. No structural changes.</design>
<acceptance>1. Per-encoder fixtures have non-zero duration_s/tokens_per_sec/llm_call_count/chunk_count after a v4 bench run.
2. Ensemble fixture has the full Phase A wall clock as its duration.
3. State Inspector center pane shows DIFFERENT mention counts per encoder card (gliner-medium 19 ≠ gliner-large 23 ≠ gliner-pii 20 etc.).
4. Consensus card has source text in the INPUT pane + consensus mentions in the OUTPUT pane.
5. Per-window cards (`:win-*`) show their assertions in the OUTPUT pane.
6. Card badges visually differentiate NER vs CONSENSUS vs WIN at a glance in the rail.
7. Smoke run produces a screenshot where each bench-table row has populated columns AND the inspector's per-encoder cards each show distinct mentions.</acceptance>
<labels>["v4", "polish", "state-inspector", "bench-table"]</labels>
</invoke>

title: Phase E: bench harness — emit per-encoder + ensemble fixtures, drive build_ensemble_pipeline
description:
Parent: CD-y4u0. Depends on Phase A (CD-7h9m), B (CD-94ow), D (CD-3w3n) — all complete.

Refactor `tests/benchmark_harness.py` to drive the v4 ensemble pipeline. Phase A of the bench (currently NER-once-per-doc with the reference encoder) becomes "run NER ensemble once per doc". The ensemble produces per-encoder mentions + consensus_mentions. The harness saves:
- One fixture per encoder (`extraction_<encoder_name>.json`) for independent F1-vs-GT scoring
- One ensemble fixture (`extraction_ensemble.json`) — competes head-to-head with single-model fixtures
- Per-SPO-model fixtures (`extraction_<spo_model>.json`) — runs SPO over consensus

This is the structural rewire that makes the new --ensemble + --spo-models CLI (CD-mjww) meaningful.

**Files:**
- `tests/benchmark_harness.py` — substantial rewrite of `_phase_a_*` and `_run_model`
- `tests/benchmark_config.py` — confirm encoder vs LLM tagging matches the new role split
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/cluster_cache.py` — cache value shape may need to extend to include `per_encoder_mentions` + `consensus_mentions` (currently caches clusters + mentions per CD-jsha)</description>
<design>**Bench flow under v4:**

```
Phase A — once across the run (cached per doc):
  for each doc:
    ensemble_pipeline.ainvoke({raw_text, doc_id, ...})
      → state.per_encoder_mentions: dict[encoder, list[mention]]
      → state.consensus_mentions: list[ConsensusMention]
      → state.entity_clusters
      → state.evidence_windows
    Save:
      - extraction_<encoder>.json per encoder (mention_count, mentions[])
      - extraction_ensemble.json (consensus mentions[] with full provenance)
      - cluster_cache entry includes per_encoder_mentions + consensus + clusters + windows

Phase B — per SPO model in --spo-models:
  for each spo_model:
    set LLM_MODEL=spo_model
    for each doc:
      use cached evidence_windows + consensus_mentions
      for each window:
        spo_pipeline.ainvoke(window with consensus mentions in upstream_context)
    Save: extraction_<spo_model>.json (assertions[])
```

**Encoders are NOT in the SPO loop**: they don't do SPO. Their fixture is purely from Phase A. SPO models are LLMs that consume consensus.

**Cluster cache schema extension:**
Currently caches `CachedNerResult{clusters, mentions}` per CD-jsha. Extend to:
```python
@dataclass
class CachedNerResult:
    clusters: list[dict]       # entity_clusters (existing)
    mentions: list[dict]       # consensus_mentions (was: single-NER accepted)
    per_encoder_mentions: dict[str, list[dict]]  # NEW
    evidence_windows: list[dict]                 # NEW (avoid re-pack on Phase B)
    rejected_mentions: list[dict]                # NEW (consensus rejects)
```
Backwards-compat: legacy entries (lacking per_encoder_mentions) still load with `per_encoder_mentions={}`.

**`_phase_a_build_cluster_cache` rewrite:**
1. Use `build_ensemble_pipeline(encoders=ENCODER_CONFIGS, ...)` instead of `build_ner_pipeline`.
2. For each doc, run the ensemble pipeline once; receive ner_result with all five state fields.
3. Save per-encoder fixtures during Phase A (one per encoder, captured from `per_encoder_mentions`).
4. Save the ensemble fixture (consensus_mentions).
5. Cache `CachedNerResult` with all fields populated.

**`_run_model` rewrite:**
- Encoder/specialist tier: skip Phase B entirely. Their fixture was already saved in Phase A. Just register the result for the report.
- LLM tier: run Phase B SPO over evidence_windows from cache, with `upstream_context.accepted_mentions = window-filtered consensus_mentions`.

**Per-encoder fixture shape:**
Match existing `extraction.json` shape so the report.json builder doesn't need to change. Fields: `mentions[], assertions[]=[], stats: {mention_count, assertion_count=0, duration_s, ...}`. Each encoder is treated as "an extraction model that ran NER but no SPO" — the report row will show 0 SPO, which is correct.

**Ensemble fixture shape:**
Same shape but `mentions` are ConsensusMention dicts (with vote_count, source_models, etc. fields preserved for the bench report viewer to render the consensus detail).

**No changes to:**
- argparse / CLI flags (Phase E.5 owns that). Continue to take `--models foo,bar` for now; the harness internally splits encoders → ensemble, LLMs → spo-models based on tags. CD-mjww replaces this with explicit flags later.
- StateInspector frontend (Phase F).
- Build output / fixture saving paths.

**Tests:**
- `test_phase_a_emits_per_encoder_fixtures.py` — mock the ensemble pipeline; assert N+1 fixtures saved per doc (N encoders + 1 ensemble).
- `test_phase_b_uses_consensus_for_spo.py` — mock SPO pipeline; assert upstream_context.accepted_mentions contains ConsensusMention dicts.
- `test_cluster_cache_v4_schema.py` — round-trip CachedNerResult with per_encoder_mentions; legacy entries (without it) load with `{}`.</design>
<acceptance>1. `_phase_a_build_cluster_cache` runs `build_ensemble_pipeline` and produces all five state fields per doc.
2. Per-encoder fixtures saved (one per ensemble encoder) at `extraction_<encoder_name>.json`.
3. Ensemble fixture saved at `extraction_ensemble.json` with full ConsensusMention provenance fields.
4. Phase B (SPO) skips encoder/specialist tier models; runs only for LLM tier.
5. Phase B SPO loop populates upstream_context.accepted_mentions from window-filtered consensus_mentions.
6. ClusterCache extended schema (with per_encoder_mentions + evidence_windows + rejected_mentions); backwards-compat for legacy entries.
7. New tests pass; existing 178 exgraph + dagster-io tests still pass; module imports clean.
8. Smoke run with a tiny corpus produces correctly-shaped fixture set: 5 encoder fixtures + 1 ensemble + N SPO model fixtures.</acceptance>
<labels>["v4", "phase-e", "bench", "harness"]</labels>
</invoke>

title: Phase D: SPO prompt refactor — inject consensus metadata into Phase 4 LLM prompt
description:
Parent: CD-y4u0. Depends on Phase B (CD-94ow, complete).

The whole point of building consensus mentions with vote counts + mean confidence is so the SPO step's LLM has grounded confidence per entity. Today the SPO node receives `upstream_context.accepted_mentions` as a flat list of `{text}` strings — the consensus metadata is dropped on the floor between extract.py and the prompt template.

Refactor the SPO prompt + the upstream-context plumbing so the LLM sees per-entity provenance:
```
Entities (with NER agreement):
  - Reagan       [PERSON,        5/5 votes, mean_conf 0.94]
  - Putin        [PERSON,        4/5 votes, mean_conf 0.87]
  - Crimea       [LOCATION,      3/5 votes, mean_conf 0.62]
  - SPEAKER_07   [PERSON,        1/5 votes, mean_conf 0.41]   ← LLM should weight this lower
```

The LLM can use vote_count / mean_conf to (a) skip relations involving low-vote entities, (b) downweight propositions, or (c) flag uncertain assertions. Reduces hallucination on weakly-supported entities.

**Files:**
- Modified: `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/nodes/extract.py` — `ExtractNode` for SPO stage builds prompt context with consensus provenance
- Modified: `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/extraction.py` — `extract_validated` + `extract_with_shared_clusters` SPO loop pass full ConsensusMention objects (not just .text strings) into upstream_context
- Modified prompts: any SPO `.prompt` file under `libs/catalyst-langgraph-aio/prompts/` or `prompts/` — update the system message to teach the LLM what the vote tally means
- Modified: maybe `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/state.py` — `upstream_context` typed shape if applicable</description>
<design>**Current state** (in extract.py SPO branch, line ~85):
```python
if self.config.stage_name == "spo":
    upstream = state.get("upstream_context", {})
    accepted_mentions = upstream.get("accepted_mentions", [])
    mention_names = [m.get("text", "") for m in accepted_mentions if m.get("text")]
    prompt = f"Input mentions: {json.dumps(mention_names)}\n\nInput text: {raw_text}"
```

`mention_names` is a list of bare strings. Even when consensus is wired, the SPO LLM only sees text — no vote counts, no provenance, no confidence.

**New shape:**
```python
if self.config.stage_name == "spo":
    upstream = state.get("upstream_context", {})
    accepted_mentions = upstream.get("accepted_mentions", [])
    entity_block = _format_entity_provenance(accepted_mentions)  # NEW
    prompt = f"Entities (with NER agreement):\n{entity_block}\n\nInput text: {raw_text}"
```

Where `_format_entity_provenance(mentions)` produces:
```
- Reagan       [PERSON,        5/5 votes, mean_conf 0.94]
- Putin        [PERSON,        4/5 votes, mean_conf 0.87]
...
```

For mentions that don't carry consensus metadata (legacy single-NER pipelines), fall back to the bare-text format so existing callers don't break:
```python
def _format_entity_provenance(mentions: list[dict]) -> str:
    lines = []
    for m in mentions:
        text = m.get("text", "")
        if not text:
            continue
        # ConsensusMention shape (Phase B output)
        if "vote_count" in m and "n_encoders" in m:
            t = m.get("canonical_type", "?")
            v = m.get("vote_count", 0)
            n = m.get("n_encoders", 0)
            c = m.get("mean_confidence", 0.0)
            lines.append(f"  - {text:24} [{t}, {v}/{n} votes, mean_conf {c:.2f}]")
        else:
            # Legacy bare-mention shape — no provenance available
            t = m.get("mention_type", m.get("type", "?"))
            lines.append(f"  - {text:24} [{t}]")
    return "\n".join(lines) if lines else "  (no entities)"
```

**System prompt update:**
Find the SPO system prompt (likely `prompts/spo.prompt` or similar). Add a section:
```
The "Entities" list below comes from a consensus of N specialized NER models.
Each entity carries:
  - canonical type
  - vote_count / n_encoders — how many NER models agreed
  - mean_conf — average confidence across agreeing models

Use this signal: entities with high vote_count and high mean_conf are reliable;
entities with low vote_count (e.g. 1/5) or low mean_conf (< 0.5) are weakly
supported. Avoid generating propositions involving weakly-supported entities
unless the source text strongly justifies them. When in doubt, omit the relation
rather than fabricate one.
```

**Upstream context plumbing** (in extraction.py SPO loops):
- `extract_validated()` SPO loop builds `upstream_context = {"accepted_mentions": window_mentions}` — change `window_mentions` to be ConsensusMention objects (full dicts with vote_count etc.) when consensus is available, or fall back to legacy mention dicts.
- `extract_with_shared_clusters()` SPO loop: same change. Currently passes `accepted_mentions: []` (empty list); needs to populate from consensus mentions filtered to the window's mention_indices.

**Tests:**

- `test_spo_prompt_legacy_fallback.py` — feed bare-mention dicts; verify fallback shape (no votes pattern).
- `test_spo_upstream_context_plumbing.py` — verify extract_validated's SPO loop forwards ConsensusMention shape (full dict with vote_count) when consensus is available, not just text strings.</design>
<acceptance>1. `_format_entity_provenance` helper exists; produces the documented "X/Y votes, mean_conf Z.ZZ" format for ConsensusMentions.
2. Legacy bare-mention path still works (no crash when consensus metadata absent).

4. `extract_validated` and `extract_with_shared_clusters` forward ConsensusMention objects (not just text) into upstream_context when consensus is available.

title: Phase B: ConsensusNode + per-model type taxonomy + full audit trail per decision
description:
Parent: CD-y4u0. Depends on Phase A (CD-7h9m, complete).

Build `ConsensusNode` that consumes `state["per_encoder_mentions"]` (output of Phase A's NerEnsembleNode) and produces consensus mentions with full provenance. **Every decision (accept, reject, span pick, type vote) emits an audit event** so the State Inspector can show why a mention was kept or dropped.

**Files:**
- New: `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/nodes/consensus.py` — `ConsensusNode` class
- New: `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/consensus_taxonomy.py` — per-encoder type → canonical map
- Modified: `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/state.py` — add `ConsensusMention` TypedDict + `consensus_mentions` field
- Modified: `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/pipeline.py` — wire ConsensusNode into `build_ensemble_pipeline` between NerEnsembleNode and cluster_entities</description>
<design>**ConsensusMention TypedDict** (in state.py):
```python
class ConsensusMention(TypedDict, total=False):
    mention_id: str             # stable id derived from (canonical_text, canonical_type, span_provenance.start)
    text: str                   # canonical surface form (lowest-conf-strip-whitespace lowering)
    canonical_type: str         # post type-vote winner
    span_start: int             # from span_provenance model
    span_end: int
    span_provenance: str        # which encoder's span was used
    source_models: list[str]    # encoders that voted for this mention
    vote_count: int             # len(source_models)
    n_encoders: int             # total encoders in ensemble (denominator)
    mean_confidence: float      # mean across source_models
    type_votes: dict[str, int]  # canonical_type → vote count
    raw_mentions: list[dict]    # per-encoder source mentions (preserved for debugging)
```

**Clustering algorithm:**
For each mention across all encoders:
1. Canonicalize: `(text.lower().strip(), canonical_type, span)`
2. Group mentions where:
   - Same canonical_text AND
   - span overlap ≥ 50% (Jaccard or simple overlap_chars / max_chars)
3. Within a group: vote on type (majority on canonical types), pick span from highest-conf encoder.

**Quorum filtering:**
- Default `K = ceil(N/2)` where N = number of encoders.
- Per-type override: PII categories (PII_NAME, PII_PHONE, PII_SSN, etc.) accept K=1 (asymmetric coverage — gliner-pii is the only encoder that finds these).
- Configurable via `quorum: int | None` constructor arg + per-type dict.

**Type canonicalization** (`consensus_taxonomy.py`):
```python
TYPE_CANONICAL: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {
    "gliner-medium": {"PERSON": "PERSON", "LOC": "LOCATION", "ORG": "ORGANIZATION", ...},
    "gliner-large":  {"PERSON": "PERSON", "LOC": "LOCATION", "ORG": "ORGANIZATION", ...},
    "gliner-pii":    {"PII_NAME": "PERSON", "PII_PHONE": "PHONE_NUMBER", ...},
    "nuextract-2.0-8b": {...},
    "universalner-7b":  {...},
}
PII_TYPES: set[str] = {"PHONE_NUMBER", "EMAIL", "SSN", "CREDIT_CARD", "ADDRESS"}
```

Read from existing `MentionType` enum where possible. Unknown types pass through unchanged (logged once at WARN level).

**Audit events** (mandatory per CD-y4u0 observability requirements):
- `consensus_started` (status: started, chunk_id `{doc_id}:_consensus`) — at node entry, with details: `{n_encoders, total_input_mentions}`
- `mention_decision` (status: accepted, chunk_id `{doc_id}:_consensus`) — per accepted consensus mention, details include: `{text, canonical_type, vote_count, n_encoders, source_models, mean_confidence, type_votes, span_provenance, span_disagreement_chars (non-zero if encoders disagreed on span)}`
- `mention_rejected` (status: rejected, chunk_id `{doc_id}:_consensus`) — per rejected mention, details include: `{text, vote_count, n_encoders, quorum, reason: "below_quorum"}`. Rejected = found by some encoders but didn't reach K.
- `consensus_completed` (status: completed) — at node exit, details include: `{accepted_count, rejected_count, mean_vote_count, type_distribution{}, span_disagreement_rate}`

**Implementation sketch:**
```python
class ConsensusNode:
    def __init__(self, encoders: list[str], quorum: int | None = None, per_type_quorum: dict[str, int] | None = None):
        self.encoders = encoders
        self.n_encoders = len(encoders)
        self.default_quorum = quorum or math.ceil(self.n_encoders / 2)
        self.per_type_quorum = per_type_quorum or {t: 1 for t in PII_TYPES}

    async def __call__(self, state: ExGraphState) -> dict[str, Any]:
        per_encoder = state.get("per_encoder_mentions") or {}
        doc_id = (state.get("doc_id") or (state.get("source_metadata") or {}).get("document_id") or "")
        consensus_chunk_id = f"{doc_id}:_consensus"

        # 1. Canonicalize all mentions
        # 2. Cluster (text-lower, span overlap ≥ 50%)
        # 3. For each cluster: vote type, pick span from highest-conf, count votes
        # 4. Apply quorum (per-type override for PII)
        # 5. Emit mention_decision per accepted, mention_rejected per below-quorum
        # 6. Emit consensus_completed with summary stats
        ...
        return {"consensus_mentions": accepted, "rejected_mentions": rejected}
```

**Integration in `build_ensemble_pipeline`:**
```
ensemble_ner → consensus → cluster_entities → pack_evidence
```
The `cluster_entities` and `pack_evidence` nodes operate on `state["consensus_mentions"]` instead of the legacy single-NER `state["stages"]["ner"]["accepted"]`. Update those nodes to read `state["consensus_mentions"]` first, fall back to legacy path for non-ensemble pipelines.

**Tests:**
- `test_consensus_clustering.py`: identical (text, type) across 3 encoders → 1 cluster, vote_count=3
- `test_consensus_span_overlap.py`: same text, overlapping but not identical spans → 1 cluster (≥50% overlap)
- `test_consensus_type_voting.py`: 3 encoders disagree on type → majority wins, type_votes preserved
- `test_consensus_quorum.py`: 5 encoders, mention found by 2 → rejected (below ceil(5/2)=3); found by 3 → accepted
- `test_consensus_pii_override.py`: PHONE_NUMBER found by gliner-pii only (1/5 vote) → accepted (PII override)
- `test_consensus_audit_events.py`: each accepted mention emits mention_decision; each rejected emits mention_rejected; both have chunk_id={doc_id}:_consensus
- `test_consensus_span_provenance.py`: span chosen from highest-conf encoder; span_disagreement_chars reflects max-min span difference</design>
<acceptance>1. ConsensusNode produces ConsensusMention[] from per_encoder_mentions input.
2. Type canonicalization map covers all 5 default ensemble encoders.
3. Quorum default = ceil(N/2); per-type override for PII supported.
4. Span provenance: highest-conf encoder's span wins; disagreement size logged.
5. Every accepted mention emits mention_decision; every rejected emits mention_rejected. NO silent drops.
6. consensus_started + consensus_completed bracket the node.
7. chunk_id pattern `{doc_id}:_consensus` so State Inspector surfaces a consensus card distinct from per-encoder cards.
8. cluster_entities + pack_evidence nodes updated to read state.consensus_mentions when available.
9. All new tests pass; existing 151 tests still pass; module imports clean across 4 code locations.</acceptance>

title: Phase E.5: bench CLI redesign — drop --models, split into --ensemble + --spo-models
description:
Parent: CD-y4u0 (v4 ensemble extraction). Sequences after Phase E (bench harness rewrite).

`--models foo,bar,baz` collapses two distinct roles (NER encoder vs SPO model) into one bag, which makes no sense under v4. Replace with explicit role-split flags. **No backwards compat shim — `--models` is removed.**

**New CLI shape:**
```
task bench:run -- \
  --ensemble gliner-medium,gliner-large,gliner-pii,nuextract-2.0-8b,universalner-7b \
  --spo-models gemma3-12b,llama3.1-8b,gpt-4o-mini \
  --sample-per-domain 0 \
  --timeout 7200
```

**Files affected:**
- `tests/benchmark_harness.py` — argparse rewrite
- `Taskfile.yml` — bench:run task description / examples
- `BENCHMARK.md` — usage docs
- `docs/blog/edc-pipeline-architecture/README.md` — bench command examples</description>
<design>**Two primary flags (required):**

- `--ensemble <comma-list>` — encoders that vote in the Phase 1 NER consensus. Each ALSO produces an individual fixture (extraction_<encoder>.json) for per-model F1 vs GT scoring. Defaults to all `encoder` + `extraction-specialist`-tagged models from benchmark_config.py if omitted.

- `--spo-models <comma-list>` — models that consume the consensus output and run Phase 4 SPO per evidence window. Each produces extraction_<model>.json. Defaults to all `tier1` + `tier2` + `cloud`-tagged models if omitted (gated by API-key presence for cloud).

**Four extra knobs:**

- `--ensemble-quorum K` — override the consensus quorum threshold. Default: `ceil(N/2)` where N=len(--ensemble). Specials: `--ensemble-quorum 1` for "any encoder finds it", `--ensemble-quorum N` for "all must agree".

- `--ensemble-only` — skip Phase 4 entirely. NER bench only — produces per-encoder fixtures + ensemble fixture, no SPO. Fast iteration when tuning encoder set or quorum.

- `--spo-only` — requires `--run-id <id>` of a previous bench whose consensus was cached. Skips Phase 1+2, runs only Phase 4 against the cached consensus. SPO model iteration without re-paying NER.

- `--no-consensus` — run each `--ensemble` model as a standalone NER+SPO pipeline (the v3 fairness path). Each model produces its own NER + own clusters + own SPO. Useful for A/B comparison: "does ensemble+SPO beat single-model NER+SPO?". Mutually exclusive with `--ensemble-only` and `--spo-only`.

**`--models` removal:**
- Delete the argparse argument entirely.
- argparse error message ("unrecognized argument: --models") is sufficient; users will adapt.
- Update README + Taskfile + blog post examples in same PR.

**Validation:**
- argparse mutually-exclusive group for {`--ensemble-only`, `--spo-only`, `--no-consensus`}.
- `--spo-only` requires `--run-id`; argparse error if missing.
- Empty `--ensemble` (when no defaults match) → fail-loud error: "no ensemble encoders configured; pass --ensemble or check benchmark_config.py tags".

**Default model resolution:**
```python
def _default_ensemble() -> list[str]:
    return [m.name for m in ALL_MODELS if "encoder" in m.tags or "extraction-specialist" in m.tags]

def _default_spo() -> list[str]:
    return [m.name for m in ALL_MODELS if any(t in m.tags for t in ("tier1", "tier2", "cloud"))]
```

**Bench fixture layout (under each run):**
```
bench/runs/<run_id>/
├── extraction_gliner-medium.json     ← per-encoder
├── extraction_gliner-large.json
├── extraction_gliner-pii.json
├── extraction_nuextract-2.0-8b.json
├── extraction_universalner-7b.json
├── extraction_ensemble.json          ← consensus
├── extraction_gemma3-12b.json        ← per-SPO-model (over consensus)
├── extraction_llama3.1-8b.json
├── extraction_gpt-4o-mini.json
├── consensus.json                    ← raw consensus output (cached for --spo-only reruns)
└── benchmark-report.json             ← per-fixture rows + ensemble row
```</design>
<acceptance>1. `--models` argument removed; argparse rejects it with a clear "use --ensemble + --spo-models" hint in the bench:run desc.
2. `--ensemble` + `--spo-models` accept comma-lists and resolve defaults from benchmark_config tags when omitted.
3. `--ensemble-quorum` overrides consensus K (validated 1 ≤ K ≤ N).
4. `--ensemble-only` produces NER fixtures + ensemble fixture, exits before Phase 4.
5. `--spo-only --run-id <id>` loads cached consensus, runs Phase 4 only, requires --run-id.
6. `--no-consensus` runs each ensemble model as a standalone NER+SPO pipeline; mutually exclusive with --ensemble-only and --spo-only.
7. Taskfile.yml + BENCHMARK.md + blog post examples updated.
8. Smoke run with `--ensemble-only --sample-per-domain 5` produces correct fixture set.</acceptance>

class NerEnsembleNode:

        # clients: pre-resolved clients keyed by encoder name

title: EPIC: NER ensemble + consensus → SPO with provenance metadata (v4 extraction)
description:
v3's "single reference NER → SPO" design has two problems: (1) it makes NER bench comparison meaningless (every model returns the reference's mentions); (2) production loses recall by relying on a single encoder when an ensemble would catch substantially more.

**v4 design**: replace the single-NER pass with a parallel encoder ensemble + consensus + scored provenance, then feed SPO with consensus metadata so the LLM has grounded confidence per entity.

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │  Phase 1 — NER ensemble (parallel)   │
                    │  gliner-medium ┐                     │
doc text  ────────► │  gliner-large  ├─► per-model         │
                    │  gliner-pii    ├─► mentions          │
                    │  nuextract-2   ├─►                   │
                    │  universalner  ┘                     │
                    └─────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                  ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │  Phase 2 — Consensus + scoring       │
                    │  Cluster by (text, canonical_type,   │
                    │  span overlap). Per cluster:         │
                    │   - source_models: [m1, m2, m3]      │
                    │   - vote_count: 3/5                  │
                    │   - mean_confidence: 0.79            │
                    │   - span: from highest-conf model    │
                    │   - type: majority vote on canonical │
                    │  Apply quorum threshold (default     │
                    │  ceil(N/2); per-type override for    │
                    │  PII at 1/N).                        │
                    └─────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                  ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │  Phase 3 — Cluster + pack            │
                    │  (proximity + Qwen3 embed-merge,     │
                    │   on consensus mentions, unchanged   │
                    │   from v3 cluster_entities/pack)     │
                    └─────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                  ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │  Phase 4 — SPO per evidence window   │
                    │  Prompt includes consensus metadata: │
                    │   "Entities (NER votes / mean conf): │
                    │    - Reagan  [PERSON, 5/5, 0.94]     │
                    │    - Putin   [PERSON, 4/5, 0.87]     │
                    │    - Crimea  [LOC,    3/5, 0.62]"    │
                    │  SPO returns assertions linked to    │
                    │  canonical entity ids; LLM can       │
                    │  weight proposition confidence by    │
                    │  vote_count / mean_conf.             │
                    └─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Why** (vs v3 single-NER):
- **Bench fairness**: each NER encoder is compared on its own Phase 1 output. Ensemble result is a separate fixture compared against per-model results.
- **Recall**: gliner-pii catches PII (phones, SSNs) other models miss; universalner has different domain coverage; nuextract surfaces structured entities. Quorum'd union > any individual.
- **Provenance**: every consensus mention carries `{source_models[], vote_count, mean_conf, type_votes}`. Gold for HITL / DPO / scoring.
- **SPO grounding**: LLM weighting based on NER agreement reduces hallucinated relations on weakly-supported entities.
- **Variables isolated**: NER bench measures Phase 1 + 2 quality. SPO bench measures Phase 4 quality given identical consensus input.

**Architectural decisions (locked):**
1. Span agreement: highest-confidence model's span. Simple, defensible, preserves provenance attribute.
2. Type voting: majority vote on canonical types. Pre-step: per-model `type_canonicalize` map (e.g., `gliner-pii.PII_NAME → MentionType.PERSON`, `universalner.ENTITY → infer from context`).
3. Quorum: `K = ceil(N/2)` default, configurable per-type. PII categories allow `K=1` (asymmetric coverage).
4. Per-model fixtures saved alongside ensemble fixture so per-model F1 vs GT is computable.
5. Ensemble fixture is its own row in the bench report — competes head-to-head with single models.
6. Cluster + pack (Phase 3) operates on CONSENSUS mentions, unchanged.

**Affected:**
- New: `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/nodes/ner_ensemble.py` — `NerEnsembleNode` (parallel asyncio.gather over configured encoders).
- New: `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/nodes/consensus.py` — `ConsensusNode` (clustering + voting + span/type policies).
- New: `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/consensus_taxonomy.py` — per-model type canonicalization map.
- Modified: `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/state.py` — add `ConsensusMention` TypedDict with provenance fields.
- Modified: `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/pipeline.py` — `build_ner_pipeline` becomes `build_ensemble_pipeline` (ensemble → consensus → cluster → pack).
- Modified: `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/extraction.py` — drop `shared_mentions: dict` parameter (consensus mentions live on the cached result); SPO prompt refactor to inject consensus metadata.
- Modified: `tests/benchmark_harness.py` — Phase A runs the ensemble; emits per-model fixtures for each encoder + an ensemble fixture; Phase B per LLM/specialist runs SPO using consensus.</description>
<design>**Phases (sub-issues created separately):**

- **Phase A — NerEnsembleNode**: parallel encoder invocation, per-model mention output, audit events tagged with source_model. ~3hrs.
- **Phase B — ConsensusNode + taxonomy**: clustering by (text-lowered, canonical-type, span-overlap≥50%), voting policies, quorum threshold, span-from-highest-conf, type canonicalization map. ~4hrs.
- **Phase C — Schema + state**: `ConsensusMention` TypedDict with `source_models[]`, `vote_count`, `mean_conf`, `span_provenance`, `type_votes{}`. Update `ExGraphState` and downstream readers. ~1hr.
- **Phase D — SPO prompt refactor**: extract.py SPO node injects consensus metadata into the prompt context. Add a `_format_entity_provenance(mentions)` helper. ~2hrs.
- **Phase E — Bench harness rewrite**: Phase A runs ensemble, saves per-model + consensus fixtures. Per-model fixture lets us still bench gliner-medium vs gliner-large independently. Phase B per LLM-tier model runs SPO using consensus. Encoder-tier models skip Phase B (they don't do SPO). ~2hrs.
- **Phase F — Bench scoring + report extensions**: report.json gets a new `ensemble` row alongside per-model rows. Scoring shows ensemble's recall vs each model's recall. ~2hrs.

**Out of scope for this epic:**
- Replacing the bench's hand-rolled ClusterCache with a Dagster multi_asset (CD-1tzf) — orthogonal cleanup. v4 ensemble can ship on the existing cache; the multi_asset migration is a separate refactor.
- ML training on consensus disagreement (which would be a great DPO signal but is downstream).
- Streaming / async-yielding of partial NER results during Phase A. Synchronous gather is fine.

**Encoder set for v4:**
Default ensemble: `gliner-medium`, `gliner-large`, `gliner-pii`, `nuextract-2.0-8b`, `universalner-7b`. Configurable via `BENCH_NER_ENSEMBLE` env var (comma-separated model names from `tests/benchmark_config.py::ENCODER_MODELS`).</design>
<acceptance>1. NerEnsembleNode runs all configured encoders in parallel via asyncio.gather; per-model output preserved.
2. ConsensusNode produces ConsensusMention[] with required provenance fields.
3. Each NER model's individual fixture is saved (independent F1-vs-GT computable).
4. Ensemble fixture is its own row in benchmark-report.json.
5. SPO prompts include consensus metadata; assertions in propositions reference vote-count-aware confidences.
6. Smoke run on the existing dev corpus produces meaningfully different mention counts per encoder + a higher-recall ensemble result.
7. State Inspector renders the per-encoder NER cards distinct from the ensemble consensus card.
8. EPIC closes when all 6 phases close.</acceptance>
<labels>["extraction", "ner", "ensemble", "consensus", "v4", "epic"]</labels>
</invoke>
notes:
Observability requirements (locked): every consensus decision must flow through event_tail and be visible in the State Inspector. No silent decisions.

PER-ENCODER EVENTS (Phase A): ner_encoder_started/completed per (doc, encoder); chunk_id='{doc_id}:_ner_{encoder}'; per-encoder mention_provenance event saved.

CONSENSUS DECISIONS (Phase B): consensus_started/completed per doc. For each mention: mention_decision event with vote_count, source_models, mean_conf, type_votes, accepted/rejected reason, span_provenance. Rejected mentions get mention_rejected events. chunk_id='{doc_id}:_consensus'.

BENCH FIXTURES (Phase E): per-encoder fixture (extraction_<encoder>.json) for independent F1; ensemble fixture (extraction_ensemble.json); both compete in report.

STATE INSPECTOR (Phase F): rail shows model->domain->doc->{per-encoder cards, consensus card, per-window SPO cards}. Consensus card detail: vote breakdown, span provenance, type tally, accept/reject reason. SPO cards show consensus metadata that fed the prompt.

NO SILENT FAIL: every drop, every span disagreement, every type tie emits an audit event with the rationale.

title: [bug] Per-LLM-call timeout — wedged Ollama eats 9hr silently
description:
Bench harness `--timeout 7200` is enforced per-MODEL, not per-LLM-call. If Ollama crashes mid-bench, the SPO call hangs on a TCP read against an established-but-dead connection. Today's incident: bench started 23:03 yesterday, hung at 23:04 (48s into the run) when Ollama died, kept the python process in `S+` (sleeping on TCP) for 9.5 hours until manually killed.

**Symptoms:**
- Process state `S+` (waiting), CPU near zero
- TCP CLOSE_WAIT to localhost:11434 + ESTABLISHED but no incoming bytes
- events.jsonl mtime frozen — last event was a `chunk_loaded` from extract_with_shared_clusters entering the next evidence window
- Per-model `--timeout` never trips because the timeout is enforced by `subprocess.run(..., timeout=...)` in the legacy path, not the in-process v3 path

**Fix direction:**
1. Add explicit per-call timeout to OpenAIEmbeddings + ChatOpenAI clients in `EmbeddingResource` / `LLMResource`. The httpx client supports `timeout=` (defaults to 60s for stream, can drop to e.g. 30s connect + 120s read).
2. Add health-check ping before each evidence-window SPO call: `requests.head(f"{base_url}/models", timeout=2)` — fail fast if endpoint is dead.
3. Optional: wrap each `spo_pipeline.ainvoke` in `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=N)` so a per-window cap exists at the bench-harness level.

**Affected:**
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/llm.py` — EmbeddingResource + LLMResource client construction
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/extraction.py::extract_with_shared_clusters` — wrap spo_pipeline.ainvoke in asyncio.wait_for
- `tests/benchmark_harness.py` — log + skip-to-next-model on per-call timeout instead of bubbling up</description>
<labels>["bench", "robustness", "v3"]</labels>
</invoke>

title: [bug] ClusterCache schema: persist mentions alongside clusters (S3 warm-cache miss path)
description:
Follow-up to CD-7bco. The mention-bubbleup fix passes Phase A NER mentions through to Phase B via `shared_mentions: dict[str, list]`, populated via a closure in `_phase_a_build_cluster_cache`. This works on cold cache (compute_fn runs, populates the closure-captured holder) and on the in-memory cache fallback. It DOES NOT work on a warm S3 ClusterCache hit — when `get_or_compute` returns cached clusters from S3, the compute_fn doesn't run, so the closure's `_doc_mentions_holder[0]` stays empty and `shared_mentions[doc_id]` becomes `[]`.

Symptom on the long real bench run with S3 cluster cache:
- First run: works correctly (cold cache, mentions captured).
- Subsequent runs across same docs: warm hit on clusters → 0 mentions → bench reports stale empty mentions.

**Fix:** persist mentions alongside clusters in the cache. Schema change.

**Affected:**
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/cluster_cache.py` — extend value shape from `list[Cluster]` to `{"clusters": [...], "mentions": [...]}`.
- `tests/benchmark_harness.py::_phase_a_build_cluster_cache` — drop the closure trick; just unpack both from the cache value.
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/extraction.py` — if `extract_with_shared_clusters` reads from cache directly anywhere, update.
- New test in `libs/dagster-io/tests/test_cluster_cache.py`: write `{clusters, mentions}` → read returns both.</description>
<design>**Schema change** (`cluster_cache.py`):

Old:
```python
def get(self, doc_id, doc_text, ner_model, params) -> list[Cluster] | None
def put(self, doc_id, doc_text, ner_model, params, clusters: list[Cluster]) -> None
def get_or_compute(self, doc_id, doc_text, ner_model, params, compute_fn: () -> list[Cluster]) -> list[Cluster]
```

New:
```python
@dataclass
class CachedNerResult:
    clusters: list[Cluster]
    mentions: list[dict]

def get(self, doc_id, doc_text, ner_model, params) -> CachedNerResult | None
def put(self, doc_id, doc_text, ner_model, params, result: CachedNerResult) -> None
def get_or_compute(self, doc_id, doc_text, ner_model, params, compute_fn: () -> CachedNerResult) -> CachedNerResult
```

**Backwards-compat read path:** if existing cache value is the old shape (a JSON list of clusters, not a dict), interpret as `clusters=value, mentions=[]` and return that — first warm hit will have empty mentions for those docs (acceptable degradation), subsequent puts use new shape.

**Storage layout:** parquet schema for cluster cache has `clusters: string` (JSON-serialized) — extend to `{"clusters": "...", "mentions": "..."}` in the same row. Or just JSON.dumps the whole CachedNerResult and store as one column. Pick whichever matches the existing pattern in `cluster_cache.py`.

**Bench harness simplification** (`_phase_a_build_cluster_cache`): drop the `_doc_mentions_holder` closure — just call `cache.get_or_compute(...)` returning `CachedNerResult`, then `cluster_by_doc[doc.doc_id] = result.clusters; mentions_by_doc[doc.doc_id] = result.mentions`.

**`_run_ner_and_cluster`** now returns `CachedNerResult` directly instead of a tuple.</design>
<acceptance>1. ClusterCache value shape is `CachedNerResult` (or equivalent); both clusters and mentions are persisted.
2. Backwards-compat: reading an old-shape cache entry doesn't crash; mentions degrade gracefully to empty for those entries (one round of staleness, then puts use new shape).
3. Bench harness reads mentions from cache on warm hit — no closure tricks remaining.
4. Smoke: run bench twice on the same corpus; second run is fast (warm cache) AND reports the same mention count as the first.
5. Existing in-memory test path still passes.
6. New test verifying mentions round-trip through put → get.</acceptance>
<labels>["bench", "cluster-cache", "v3"]</labels>
</invoke>

ClusterCache value shape is now CachedNerResult (libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/cluster_cache.py:53) carrying clusters + mentions + v4 per-encoder fields with documented bwd-compat read for legacy bare-list entries. Closure trick is gone; harness reads mentions directly from cached.mentions at tests/benchmark_harness.py:183. Round-trip covered by libs/dagster-io/tests/test_cluster_cache_v4_schema.py.

title: [bug] Phase A NER mentions don't bubble up to final extraction output (0 mentions reported)
description:
After v3 + bench-fix-v3, every model reports 0 mentions even though Phase A ran NER and produced clusters successfully. Looking at the smoke run:

```
extraction  0 mentions · 12 assertions · 45 chunks processed
```

Encoders (which only do NER, no SPO) all show 0/0. llama3.1-8b shows 0 NER but 12 SPO — meaning SPO ran on cached evidence windows but the NER mentions from Phase A never made it back to the final accumulator.

Likely cause: `extract_with_shared_clusters()` in `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/extraction.py` is the new entry point (Phase 3, CD-80ic) that bench harness calls after Phase A. It runs SPO-only per evidence window, but doesn't appear to thread Phase A's NER mentions through to the returned mention list. The cached `entity_clusters` reference NER mentions by index, but the harness needs to ALSO carry those mentions out to the final extraction set so scoring sees them.

Smoke evidence: bench run 2026-05-03-045120 shows 9 docs, 9 clusters, 12 SPO assertions, 0 NER mentions. The clusters had to come from something — either Phase A's NER ran but its mentions were discarded, or `extract_with_shared_clusters` skips re-emitting them.

Fix direction: in `extract_with_shared_clusters`, accept the Phase A NER mentions (or re-fetch them from the cached state) and include them in the returned `mention_models` list. The Phase 3 design did intend for the NER pass to be "shared" — but "shared" means the NER work is done once and reused, not that the resulting mentions vanish.

Blocks the real long bench from being meaningful — without mentions, scoring against GT is impossible.</description>
<labels>["bench", "v3", "phase-3", "bug"]</labels>
</invoke>

Bench reports non-zero NER counts on v4.

title: Phase 2: ExGraph topology rewrite — entity-anchored flow with cluster + pack nodes
description:
**Parent epic**: CD-rwlq.

Replace the linear NER||SPO topology with the entity-anchored flow. Add `cluster_entities` + `pack_evidence` nodes between NER and SPO. Rewire `extract_validated()` to outer-driver fan-out: NER once per doc, then N SPO sub-graph invocations per evidence window.

**Topology change** (current → new):

Current (`libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/pipeline.py`):
```
extract_ner → validate_ner → repair_ner ─┐
                                         ├─→ persist_artifacts
extract_spo → validate_spo → repair_spo ─┘
```

New:
```
extract_ner → validate_ner → repair_ner
                  │
                  ▼
        ┌─────────────────┐
        │ cluster_entities│  (NEW — proximity + Qwen3-8B embedding-merge)
        └─────────────────┘
                  │
                  ▼
        ┌─────────────────┐
        │ pack_evidence   │  (NEW — pack each cluster to MODEL_WINDOWS[model])
        └─────────────────┘
                  │  (outer driver loops over evidence_windows here)
                  ▼  (fan-out: extract_validated re-invokes SPO sub-graph per window)
        extract_spo → validate_spo → repair_spo  (per evidence window)
                  │
                  ▼
            persist_artifacts (per doc, after all windows complete)
```

**Why outer driver fan-out**: cleaner audit log (one ExGraph run per evidence window), the StateInspector chunk timeline shows one card per window, parallelizable across windows independently.

**Files affected:**
- `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/nodes/cluster.py` (new) — `ClusterEntitiesNode`
- `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/nodes/pack.py` (new) — `PackEvidenceNode`
- `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/pipeline.py` — split into `build_ner_pipeline()` + `build_spo_pipeline()`; remove combined `build_pipeline()`
- `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/state.py` — add `entity_clusters: list[Cluster]`, `evidence_windows: list[EvidenceWindow]` to ExGraphState
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/extraction.py` — `extract_validated()` becomes the outer driver: load doc → run NER pipeline once → cluster → pack → loop over windows running SPO pipeline → persist
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/bench/event_tail.py` — emit per-evidence-window events tagged with `evidence_window_id` so StateInspector groups them properly</description>
<design>**ClusterEntitiesNode** (hybrid):
1. **Proximity pass**: scan accepted_mentions in doc-char order; entities within `proximity_radius_tokens` (default 200) of each other join a cluster. Linear-time sweep using a sliding window.
2. **Embedding merge**: for each cluster, build a context window (±50 tokens around the cluster's bounding span) and embed it with Qwen3-8B via EmbeddingResource. Compute pairwise cosine; merge clusters with similarity > threshold (default 0.75) AND share at least one entity by surface form. The shared-entity check prevents merging unrelated topics that happen to be embedding-similar.
3. Emits a `clustered` event with cluster count, pre/post merge counts, plus the cluster spans for the StateInspector.

**PackEvidenceNode**:
1. Takes `entity_clusters` + `state.model` (so it knows the target window).
2. For each cluster, build an evidence window: text from `min(span_start) - context_tokens // 2` to `max(span_end) + context_tokens // 2`, clipped to doc bounds.
3. If the window exceeds `MODEL_WINDOWS[state.model]`, split greedily on sentence boundaries.
4. Output: `evidence_windows: list[{window_id, doc_char_start, doc_char_end, text, mention_ids: [...], context_tokens_used}]`.
5. Emits a `packed` event with window count, total tokens, mean tokens-per-window.

**State schema additions** (`state.py`):
```python
class EntityCluster(TypedDict):
    cluster_id: str
    mention_ids: list[str]  # references into stages.ner.accepted
    doc_char_start: int     # bounding box of the cluster
    doc_char_end: int

class EvidenceWindow(TypedDict):
    window_id: str
    doc_char_start: int
    doc_char_end: int
    text: str
    mention_ids: list[str]
    cluster_id: str
    parent_chunk_id: str    # for back-references in the audit
```

**Outer driver flow** (`extract_validated()`):
```python
for doc in docs:
    # NER pass over the full doc — chunked internally if needed
    ner_state = await ner_graph.ainvoke({"raw_text": doc.text, "doc_id": doc.id, ...})
    # Cluster + pack
    windows = ner_state["evidence_windows"]
    # SPO fan-out
    for w in windows:
        spo_state = await spo_graph.ainvoke({
            "raw_text": w["text"],
            "doc_id": doc.id,
            "evidence_window_id": w["window_id"],
            "upstream_context": {"accepted_mentions": [ner_state.mentions[i] for i in w["mention_ids"]]},
            ...
        })
        all_propositions.extend(spo_state["accepted_propositions"])
    # Persist once per doc
    persist(doc.id, all_mentions, all_propositions)
```

**Event tagging**: existing event_tail emit gets a new optional field `evidence_window_id`. NER events have it null (NER is doc-scoped); SPO events have it set. StateInspector groups by evidence_window_id when present.

**StateInspector impact**: chunk timeline becomes evidence-window timeline. Most of the recent UI work transfers — chunks → windows is a renaming. Right pane shows window provenance (cluster id, member mentions, doc_char_range, cluster size).

**Tests:**
1. `test_cluster_proximity.py`: 3 entities at chars 100, 150, 800 → two clusters {100,150} and {800}.
2. `test_cluster_embedding_merge.py`: clusters with similar contexts but different positions get merged when they share entities.
3. `test_pack_window_size.py`: gemma3 packs differently than gliner-medium for the same cluster set.
4. `test_outer_driver_fanout.py`: a doc with 3 windows triggers exactly 3 SPO sub-graph invocations; events.jsonl shows 3 distinct evidence_window_ids.</design>
<acceptance>1. `extract_validated()` runs NER once per doc, then SPO N times per doc (one per evidence window); audit log shows the fan-out.
2. ClusterEntitiesNode emits `clustered` event per doc with pre/post merge counts.
3. PackEvidenceNode emits `packed` event per doc with window count + mean tokens.
4. SPO call count drops materially (target: ~1/3 of current per the epic acceptance).
5. StateInspector renders evidence windows as chunk timeline cards with cluster provenance in the right pane.
6. wikileaks-cable-1985USUN02134 example produces ≥1 proposition (was 0).
7. Joe-rogan greeting chunks (now cluster-zero docs) skip SPO entirely (no calls, no events) — visible as "0 windows" in the timeline header.</acceptance>
<labels>["chunking", "exgraph", "v3", "phase-2"]</labels>
</invoke>

title: Phase 1: Local Qwen3-Embedding-8B backend + Ollama preset for EmbeddingResource
description:
**Parent epic**: CD-rwlq.

Add `provider="local"` to EmbeddingResource using sentence-transformers + MPS for Qwen3-Embedding-8B @ 2048 dims. Add `provider="ollama"` preset for fast local secondary. S3-cache entity-context embeddings keyed by `sha256(text + model + dim)` so the expensive doc-level pass runs once per doc.

Hardware target: M5 Max, 128 GB unified memory. Run fp16 directly without quantization. Batch size 16 for the 8B; tune up if memory allows.

**Files affected:**
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/llm.py` — extend EmbeddingResource provider switch
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/embedding_cache.py` (new) — S3-backed cache layer, keyed by content hash
- `libs/dagster-io/pyproject.toml` — add `sentence-transformers>=3.0`, `torch>=2.4` (for MPS), bgptional `transformers` direct dep for Qwen3
- `pyproject.toml` (root) — register the dep at workspace level
- Definitions wiring stays unchanged (EnvVar already in place from CD-27ba)

**Provider table (final):**
| `provider` | base_url default | model default | use case |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | `text-embedding-3-small` | API or LiteLLM passthrough |
| `litellm` | `LITELLM_BASE_URL` env / `http://litellm:4000/v1` | configurable | LiteLLM proxy preset |
| `ollama` | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | `nomic-embed-text` | fast local dev |
| `local` | n/a | `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B` | top-quality local; MPS+sentence-transformers |</description>
<design>**Local provider impl** (`setup_for_execution`):
```python
if self.provider == "local":
    import torch
    from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
    self._st_model = SentenceTransformer(
        self.model,
        device="mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu",
        model_kwargs={"torch_dtype": torch.float16},
    )
    # Matryoshka: encode at native dim, slice to self.dimensions
    # Qwen3-8B native is 4096; we slice to 2048 by default
```

**`embed()` flow for local:**
```python
def _embed_local(self, texts):
    vectors = self._st_model.encode(
        texts,
        batch_size=self.batch_size or 16,
        normalize_embeddings=True,
        convert_to_numpy=True,
        show_progress_bar=False,
    )
    target_dim = self.dimensions or 2048
    if vectors.shape[1] > target_dim:
        vectors = vectors[:, :target_dim]
        vectors = vectors / np.linalg.norm(vectors, axis=1, keepdims=True)  # re-normalize after truncation
    return vectors.tolist()
```

**Instruction-aware encoding** (Qwen3 expects this):
- For documents (encode-time): plain text, no instruction prefix.
- For queries (query-time): `"Instruct: <task description>\nQuery: <text>"` — but for our entity-clustering use case we treat all entity-context windows as documents; no instruction prefix needed at first. Add optional `instruction` field if a downstream task wants it.

**S3 cache layer** (`embedding_cache.py`):
```python
def get_or_compute(texts: list[str], model: str, dim: int, fn: Callable) -> list[list[float]]:
    """Look up each text in s3://dagster/silver/embedding_cache/<hash>.parquet.
    Compute and cache misses. Returns vectors in input order."""
    keys = [sha256(f"{model}:{dim}:{text}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16] for text in texts]
    # Batch get from S3 by listing parquet files, fall back to compute for missing
    ...
```
Use parquet for efficient batch I/O — one file per ~100 cached entries, not one file per cached entry. Read on cache miss, append on cache write.

**Ollama provider preset:**
```python
elif self.provider == "ollama":
    base_url = self.base_url or os.environ.get("OLLAMA_BASE_URL", "http://localhost:11434/v1")
    self._embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(
        base_url=base_url,
        api_key="ollama",
        model=self.model,
        chunk_size=self.batch_size or 100,
    )
```

**Tests:**
1. `test_embedding_resource_local.py`: load Qwen3-8B, embed 3 strings, verify 2048-dim output, verify cosine similarity is plausibly different for different inputs.
2. `test_embedding_resource_ollama.py`: skip-if-not-available; if Ollama is running, embed 3 strings via the preset.
3. `test_embedding_cache.py`: write-then-read returns same vectors; cache miss triggers fn; partial-hit batches correctly.</design>
<acceptance>1. `provider="local"` works end-to-end for `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B` on M5 Max via MPS, returns 2048-dim normalized vectors.
2. `provider="ollama"` preset works against a running Ollama with `nomic-embed-text`.
3. `provider="litellm"` preset works against the existing LiteLLM proxy.
4. S3 embedding cache reduces a re-run of the same doc to <100 ms for the embedding step (vs. multi-second on a fresh run).
5. Three unit tests pass; integration smoke run against a small fixture doc emits valid vectors.
6. EmbeddingResource Dagster launchpad UI still surfaces every field via EnvVar from CD-27ba.</acceptance>

title: Phase 0: Span-anchored GT migration (chunker-agnostic GT format)
description:
**Parent epic**: CD-rwlq (v3 chunking + graph topology upgrade)

Migrate GT format from chunk-keyed to doc-char-range-keyed so it survives any future chunker change. This is a Phase 0 prerequisite for the v3 topology rewrite — without it, the chunker swap orphans every existing GT entry.

**Today's GT shape:**
```json
{"chunk_id": "joe-rogan-2284:chunk-7", "text": "...", "mentions": [{span_start, span_end, ...}], "propositions": [...]}
```
Mentions carry chunk-relative spans; join key is chunk_id.

**New shape:**
```json
{
  "doc_id": "joe-rogan-2284",
  "doc_char_start": 18432,
  "doc_char_end": 19280,
  "text_excerpt": "...",
  "mentions": [{doc_char_start, doc_char_end, ...}],
  "propositions": [...]
}
```
Mentions carry absolute doc-frame spans; join key is `(doc_id, IntervalTree of doc_char_range)`.

**Files affected:**
- `tests/shared/ground_truth.py` — read + score; refactor join logic
- `tests/benchmark_harness.py` — call site for GT scoring
- `packages/media-ingest/viewer-ui/src/components/benchmark/GroundTruthPanel.tsx` (or similar) — translate-on-save: SPA stores chunk-relative, save call translates to doc-frame using `chunk_char_offset` from chunking metadata
- `packages/media-ingest/src/media_ingest/viewer/routes/bench.py` — GT save endpoint translates spans
- New script: `scripts/migrate_gt_to_doc_anchored.py` — one-time migration of existing GT files in S3</description>
<design>**Translation math:**
- Forward (chunk → doc frame): `doc_char_start = chunk.metadata.chunk_char_offset + mention.span_start`
- Reverse (doc → chunk frame at score time): for each chunk, build `IntervalTree[(chunk_char_offset, chunk_char_offset + len(chunk_text))]`, query GT entries that overlap, subtract chunk_char_offset to get back to chunk-frame spans for scoring.

**Migration script logic** (`scripts/migrate_gt_to_doc_anchored.py`):
1. Iterate every GT file in `s3://dagster/bench/ground-truth/<name>.json`.
2. For each chunk_id, look up the corresponding silver chunk from `s3://dagster/silver/<code_loc>/.../<doc_id>/data.jsonl` to get `chunk_char_offset` from `metadata`.
3. Translate every mention's span_start/end by adding the offset.
4. Rewrite as new shape, save to `s3://dagster/bench/ground-truth/<name>.json` (overwrite — old shape is unrecoverable but small enough to regen if migration breaks).
5. Backup originals to `s3://dagster/bench/ground-truth/_backup_pre_v3/<name>.json` before overwriting.

**Scoring update** (`tests/shared/ground_truth.py`):
- Build `doc_id → IntervalTree` once per doc.
- `score_chunk(chunk, gt_index)`: compute chunk's doc-char range from `metadata.chunk_char_offset` + len. Query overlapping GT. Subtract offset from each GT mention to get chunk-frame spans. Compare with model output.
- Edge case: GT entry overlaps multiple chunks (chunker overlap region). Score against the chunk with the largest overlap. Tag the duplicate cases for diagnostic logging.

**Tests required:**
1. Unit: span translator round-trip (chunk → doc → chunk gives identity).
2. Unit: IntervalTree query returns the correct GT for a known chunk.
3. Integration: a GT file in old format scored against a model output produces identical precision/recall as the same GT migrated to new format scored against the same model output. Same chunker on both sides.</design>
<acceptance>1. Migration script runs end-to-end on existing GT corpus, all files converted, originals backed up.
2. New scoring code joins GT to chunks by doc_char_range; legacy chunk_id-based join is gone.
3. Round-trip test passes: same model output scored against pre-migration GT (chunk-keyed) and post-migration GT (doc-keyed) on the same chunker yields identical metrics.
4. Bench harness runs end-to-end on the new GT format with a smoke run of one model.
5. GT editor SPA save path translates chunk-relative spans to doc-frame on PUT; existing edit workflow unchanged from the operator's perspective.
6. Documentation: short note in `docs/SEED.md` or similar describing the new GT shape + the migration script.</acceptance>
<labels>["ground-truth", "chunking", "v3", "phase-0"]</labels>
</invoke>

title: EPIC: Entity-anchored chunking redesign with Qwen3-8B clustering
description:
Replace the linear NER||SPO topology with an entity-anchored flow:

```
NER over full doc → cluster entity contexts (proximity + Qwen3-8B embedding merge)
                  → pack each cluster into model-window-sized "evidence chunks"
                  → run SPO once per evidence chunk (outer driver re-invocation, fan-out per window)
                  → persist
```

**Why**: Today's flow extracts NER + SPO over the same raw chunk. Most chunks contain greeting/header noise (transcript intros, cable mastheads); SPO finds nothing because the entities and the claims linking them get split across chunk boundaries. Per State Inspector evidence: chunk 0 of `wikileaks-cable-1985USUN02134` produced 13 mentions but 0 props because the masthead labels saturated and no real claim survived intact. Joe-rogan greeting chunks produce SPEAKER_07 + "Happy Thursday" with 0 props — pure noise.

**What entity-anchored fixes**:
- NER pass 1 over full doc finds *what we care about*. Cheap encoder (GLiNER) + sliding window.
- Cluster entity contexts so each evidence window contains a topically-coherent set of mentions. Hybrid clustering: proximity-first (cheap, local), then Qwen3-8B embedding-merge across distant clusters that talk about the same entities.
- Pack each cluster into a window sized to the *target model's* context (GLiNER 320 tok, gemma3 24K tok). No more paying GLiNER's tax on gemma3.
- SPO sees only contexts with multi-entity clusters → ~3-5× fewer SPO calls, with materially better context.

**Decisions locked** (from session conversation):
- 1. Outer driver fan-out (`extract_validated()` re-invokes SPO sub-graph per window). Cleaner audit, plays nicely with the new StateInspector chunk timeline.
- 2. Hybrid clustering (proximity + Qwen3-8B embedding-merge).
- 3. No feature flag — replace existing topology directly.
- 4. Span-anchored GT (chunker-agnostic; GT keyed by doc_char_range, mentions carry absolute doc spans). Phase 0 prerequisite.
- 5. Embedder: Qwen3-Embedding-8B @ 2048 dims via sentence-transformers + MPS, on M5 Max (128 GB).</description>
<design>**Phases** (each is a sub-issue, child issues created separately):

- **Phase 0 — Span-anchored GT migration**. Refactor GT shape from chunk-keyed to doc-char-range-keyed. ~2 days. Prerequisite for everything downstream (otherwise GT orphans on the chunker swap).

- **Phase 1 — Local Qwen3-8B embedder backend**. Add `provider="local"` to EmbeddingResource using sentence-transformers + MPS + matryoshka truncation to 2048 dims. Add Ollama provider preset as fast secondary. S3-cached entity-context embeddings. ~1 day.

- **Phase 2 — ExGraph topology rewrite**. Add `cluster_entities` + `pack_evidence` nodes between NER and SPO. Rewire `extract_validated()` to outer-driver fan-out: NER once per doc → cluster → N SPO sub-graph invocations per doc. Keep stage events flowing into events.jsonl per evidence window. ~2-3 days.

- **Phase 3 — Per-model window sizing**. Add `MODEL_WINDOWS` registry; chunker packs evidence per `model_name`. Bench harness re-chunks per-model from a single embedding cache. ~1 day.

- **Phase 4 — GT regen + bench validation**. Regen ground-truth corpus on the new chunker output. Verify scoring matches expected ranges. Ship.

**Cost cache strategy**: sentence/entity-context embeddings keyed by `sha256(text + model + dim)`, stored at `s3://dagster/silver/<code_loc>/embedding_cache/<hash>.parquet`. One Qwen3-8B pass per doc; N cheap pack steps per (doc, model).

**Topology migration is destructive** — existing benchmark runs become incomparable. We keep the old report.json files in S3 (not deleting); new runs use the new topology.</design>
<acceptance>1. Phase 0-4 sub-issues created and closed.
2. Bench reruns end-to-end with the new topology, no green-on-empty SPO results.
3. Wikileaks cable chunk 0 (the example) shows ≥1 proposition with the new chunker (vs 0 today).
4. Joe-rogan greeting chunks show ≤2 mentions and 0 props (proper rejection of noise — was 2 mentions today, but they were diarization-label garbage).
5. Per-model SPO call count drops to ~1/3 of current (with reasoning: most evidence windows have no extractable claims, those get skipped, vs. today's "run SPO over every chunk regardless").
6. GT files have new schema; existing scoring still works on regenerated GT.</acceptance>
<labels>["chunking", "extraction", "qwen3", "platform", "epic"]</labels>
</invoke>
