title: Fix env-var-as-default antipattern in all ConfigurableResource classes
description:
Every ConfigurableResource in the repo uses `os.environ.get(...)` as the field default. This evaluates ONCE at module import time, so:

1. The Dagster launchpad UI shows the literal baked-in string (e.g. "openai", "gpt-4o-mini") and has no idea those came from env vars — config is invisible/un-overridable in the UI.
2. Changing an env var requires restarting dagster-webserver to pick it up.
3. Per-run launchpad overrides have no effect on values read at import time elsewhere.
4. The Definitions blocks call `EmbeddingResource()` etc. with NO args — relying entirely on the import-time env shadow.

**Affected resources (6 classes, ~34 env-var defaults):**
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/llm.py:97` LLMResource (17 env vars)
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/llm.py:411` EmbeddingResource (6 env vars)
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/chunking.py:159` ChunkingResource (2)
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/embedding_config.py:75` EmbeddingConfigResource (3)
- `libs/catalyst-exgraph/src/catalyst_exgraph/resource.py:98` ExtractionResource (4)
- `packages/knowledge-graph/src/knowledge_graph/resources.py:62` GraphDBResource (8)

**Affected Definitions blocks (need EnvVar wiring):**
- `packages/media-ingest/src/media_ingest/__init__.py:62`
- `packages/congress-data/src/congress_data/__init__.py:76`
- `packages/open-leaks/src/open_leaks/__init__.py:37`
- `packages/knowledge-graph/src/knowledge_graph/__init__.py:84`</description>
<design>**Pattern (Dagster-idiomatic):**

1. **Strip `os.environ.get(...)` from field defaults.** Replace with plain Pydantic defaults (sane fallback values, or `None` for required fields like `api_key`).

2. **Wire `EnvVar` at Definitions construction time:**
```python
from dagster import Definitions, EnvVar
resources={
    "embeddings": EmbeddingResource(
        provider=EnvVar("EMBEDDING_PROVIDER"),
        base_url=EnvVar("EMBEDDING_BASE_URL"),
        api_key=EnvVar("EMBEDDING_API_KEY"),
        model=EnvVar("EMBEDDING_MODEL"),
        dimensions=EnvVar.int("EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS"),
        batch_size=EnvVar.int("EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE"),
    ),
}
```

3. **Use `EnvVar.int` / `EnvVar.bool`** for non-string fields so Dagster validates at run-launch time.

4. **For optional env vars**: make field type `T | None` with default `None`; resolve in `setup_for_execution` to a model-appropriate fallback. Prevents launchpad showing missing-env errors for optional knobs.

5. **Same pattern across all 6 resources** — consistent treatment so the UI is uniform.

**Net effect**: launchpad UI shows `{env: EMBEDDING_PROVIDER}` per field with an Override button. Operators can reconfigure per-run without redeploying.

**LiteLLM note**: no code change needed for LiteLLM — `provider="openai"` + `base_url=<litellm-url>` already works (LiteLLM exposes OpenAI-compatible HTTP). Optionally add a `litellm` provider preset that pre-fills the base_url for ergonomics.

**Do NOT**: change asset code, change Resource public APIs (just defaults), or change the eager-vs-lazy semantics of `setup_for_execution`. This is a config-plumbing fix only.</design>
<acceptance>1. All 6 ConfigurableResource classes have plain Pydantic defaults — zero `os.environ.get(...)` in field declarations.
2. All 4 Definitions blocks use `EnvVar(...)` (or `EnvVar.int`, `EnvVar.bool`) for every field that was previously env-driven.
3. `task dev:dagster` boots without errors.
4. Dagster launchpad UI for any asset materialization shows resource config grouped per resource, with `{env: VAR_NAME}` annotations and Override buttons (verified via Playwright snapshot).
5. Setting `EMBEDDING_MODEL=foo` in the env, then changing it in the launchpad UI to `bar` per-run, results in `bar` being used at execution time (not `foo`).
6. Existing assets still materialize end-to-end (smoke: `task seed:media` succeeds).
7. No env var loss — every previously-supported env var still drives the same field via EnvVar.</acceptance>
<labels>["dagster", "resources", "config", "platform"]</labels>
</invoke>

title: Live bench events — SSE fallback so Vite restart isn't required
description:
Bench harness's RunBus serves events on a WebSocket port discovered via .test-output/media-ingest/bench-cache/.bus-port. Vite proxies /viewer/bus → that port, BUT Vite reads .bus-port ONLY at startup. If a bench starts AFTER Vite booted, the proxy is dead — SPA's WS fails, useRunStream falls back to archived events.jsonl in S3 which doesn't exist mid-run. State Inspector + Audit Viewer show empty mid-run.

Fix: add /viewer/api/bench/events/live SSE endpoint to viewer/routes/bench.py that tails the local file at <bench_cache>/events.jsonl. SPA's useRunStream tries SSE before WS so live events flow through regular /viewer/api/* (which Vite proxies correctly to viewer-api) — no Vite-time port resolution required.

There is no Vite WS proxy or .bus-port file anymore — the underlying stale-proxy problem cannot recur.

title: GLiNER silently drops entities past 384 tokens — sliding-window the input
description:
GLiNER's preprocessor emits a UserWarning ('Sentence of length 1054 has been truncated to 384') per chunk longer than 384 tokens. The truncation is REAL data loss — entities in the back half of a multi-paragraph chunk are never seen by the model, so the encoder benchmarks systematically underreport mention counts on long chunks (Joe Rogan transcripts, FAA Reauthorization Act sections, etc.).

Two fixes needed:

(1) Update tests/benchmark_config.py: gliner-medium / gliner-large / gliner-pii entries claim context_window=512 but the architecture caps at 384. Change to 384 (or the safe-input cap, e.g. 340 once we account for special tokens).

(2) Sliding-window in libs/catalyst-langgraph-aio/src/catalyst_langgraph/clients/gliner.py — when input >~340 tokens:
  - Split into overlapping windows (340 tokens body + 40 token overlap) on sentence boundaries when possible
  - Call model.predict_entities() per window
  - Adjust each entity's span_start/span_end by the window's offset
  - Dedupe by (text, label, char_offset) when entities appear in the overlap region
  - Concat into a single result list

Acceptance: bench run on a 1000-token chunk should show 2-3x more mentions for GLiNER models vs the current truncated run. Validate by re-running gliner-medium on demo-video and checking mention_count delta.

Out of scope: NuExtract/UniversalNER may have similar behavior — track separately if their own warnings show up.
close_reason: Fixed in commit ed2ef3c (fix(viewer): GLiNER sliding window + S3 thumbnail cache + canonical media paths). Sliding-window over the 384-token cap is in the GLiNER client now.

title: Investigate guardrails against runaway LLM retry loops (cost risk)
description: On 2026-04-29, Dagster run da9216c7-e335-4518-9d26-281319e27d3d (media_ingest ASSET_JOB) got stuck for 2d2h hammering litellm with the dead model runpod/qwen3:30b-a3b. Two step pods (media_assertions, media_mentions) plus the run pod stayed alive the entire time, infinite-retrying through 404 (endpoint not found) → 429 (RouterRateLimitError, no deployments available) until manually killed via 'kubectl delete job'. Pod-level kills were ineffective because the K8s Job controller respawned them. This represents real cost risk if a runpod endpoint goes 404 mid-run on any production-scale workload. Investigate the best layered remedy across three surfaces and pick the cheapest defense-in-depth combo.
design:
Three surfaces to evaluate, ranked by likely cost-effectiveness:

(a) LiteLLM config (catalyst-llm namespace) — add fallback model group OR shrink cooldown→eviction so a 404 deployment is removed from rotation instead of returning 429 forever. Cheapest to implement, blocks the bleed at the proxy.

(b) Extraction nodes (catalyst-exgraph, catalyst-langgraph-aio) — wrap LLM calls with a circuit breaker that raises after K consecutive provider 404s within W seconds. Prevents per-node infinite retry even if litellm misbehaves.

(c) Dagster run-monitor — set step retry caps and/or ttl_seconds_after_finished + max-runtime tags on jobs that call LLMs. Belt-and-suspenders: even if (a) and (b) miss, the step gets killed by Dagster.

Investigation should produce a short ADR comparing the three, then implement the smallest combination that gives defense-in-depth. Likely answer: (a) + (b), with (c) as a hard ceiling.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Decision recorded on which layer(s) to harden (litellm config / extraction nodes / dagster run-monitor) and why.
2. LiteLLM: fallback group OR auto-removal for persistently-failing deployments configured (or a documented reason not to).
3. Extract/repair/validate nodes: circuit breaker or max-retry-with-giveup on persistent provider 404/429 so a dead model fails the step instead of looping.
4. Dagster: bounded step/run retry budget so a stuck job cannot survive >N minutes of repeated provider failures.
5. Alerting: a metric or log-based alert that fires when a step pod issues >N retries against the same model in a window.
6. Doc/runbook entry covering 'how to kill a stuck Dagster run' (delete Job, not pod; terminate via GraphQL if daemon hasn't reaped it).
notes:
Incident reference:
- Run: da9216c7-e335-4518-9d26-281319e27d3d, ASSET_JOB / media_ingest
- Stuck steps: media_assertions, media_mentions
- Model: runpod/qwen3:30b-a3b (litellm cooldown deployment 70a2584a-46b8-43a2-99fd-a75a7919eb80)
- Resolution: kubectl delete job (3 jobs); daemon auto-marked run FAILURE
- Killing pods alone had no effect — Job controller respawns them, and that gotcha needs to be in the runbook.

- prod: MinioIOManager → s3://catalyst-data/gold/media_ingest/.../media_chunks/<partition>/data.jsonl

title: Implement NuExtract + Gemma 4 model split with P-Strategy prompts
description:
Switch from single qwen3:30b-a3b for all LLM extraction to a two-model strategy based on LLMStructBench findings (https://arxiv.org/html/2602.14743v1).

Model split:
- NER/Mentions: NuExtract-2.0-8B (purpose-built extractor, highest F1 on NER benchmarks)
- Assertions/SPO: Gemma 4 27B (best open-source for structured reasoning)
- Embeddings: nomic-embed-text (unchanged)

Deployment:
- NuExtract-2.0-8B on Mac M3 via Ollama (small enough to run alongside nomic-embed-text)
- Gemma 4 27B on RunPod serverless (needs GPU)
- Add both to LiteLLM config with endpoint/model naming convention

Prompt improvements (from LLMStructBench P-Strategy):
- Include JSON schema explicitly in system prompt
- Provide concrete input→output examples (few-shot)
- Keep schemas flat (depth ≤3)
- Focus on value accuracy not schema compliance
- Add congress-specific entity type guidance with examples
- Add SPO direction examples (Sponsor→sponsors→Bill, NOT Bill→was sponsored by→Bill)

Post-processing:
- Deduplicate mentions by span
- Filter self-referential assertions (subject == object)
- Normalize predicate direction
- Filter immaterial assertions (confidence < 0.7)

Applies to both congress-data AND media-ingest pipelines.
design:
1. Pull models: ollama pull nuextract (Mac), set up Gemma 4 on RunPod

title: 5 killer validation Cypher queries as test suite
description:
Implement and validate all 5 killer queries against the Neo4j graph as a pytest test suite. Each query must return results (non-empty) against a seeded test graph or the live 119th Congress data.

1. Bipartisan bills that stalled in committee — needs COSPONSORED edges with party (via MEMBER_OF temporal), Action nodes with no floor-action terminal
2. Members whose floor votes diverge from cosponsorship — needs VOTED edges + COSPONSORED on same Member-Bill pair (depends on CD-jdc vote ingest)
3. Amendments by freshmen to climate bills — needs Term (first term = terms_served=1), PolicyArea, SPONSORED_AMENDMENT edges
4. Text drift introduced→enacted — needs BillVersion chain (ih→enr), PublicLaw terminal
5. LLM mentions of senator not in structured sponsors — needs Mention→EntityCandidate→CanonicalEntity→Person→Member traversal vs SPONSORED/COSPONSORED edges

Each query must be a parameterized Cypher function callable from the API or notebooks.

VOTED edge: Member→RollCallVote with position (Yea/Nay/Present/Not Voting). ON edge: RollCallVote→Bill (or Amendment). Enables killer query #2: compare VOTED positions against COSPONSORED edges for divergence analysis.

Beta, covers 118th+119th only. NO House Clerk XML needed. (2) Senate votes via Senate LIS XML at senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/ — API has NO Senate vote endpoint. Build parser for Senate XML only. Create RollCallVote + VOTED entities. Map roll calls to bills via vote question text + bill number. New assets: house_roll_calls (bronze, unpartitioned, from API), senate_roll_calls (bronze, unpartitioned, from Senate LIS XML), bill_votes (partitioned per bill, joins positions to bill). title: Neo4j graph write: Member + Term + Party + State + Committee nodes + edges

Edges: HELD_TERM, IN_CHAMBER, REPRESENTS (Term→District/State), MEMBER_OF (temporal, start_date/end_date), SITS_ON (temporal, role/congress). Sponsorship edges: SPONSORED (Member→Bill), COSPONSORED (Member→Bill, date/withdrawn_date/is_original).

title: Neo4j graph write: Bill + Action + BillVersion + Amendment + PolicyArea + Subject nodes

BillVersion: MERGE on bill_id:version_code. Amendment: MERGE on id. PolicyArea: MERGE on name (~32 controlled vocab). Subject: MERGE on name. Edges: HAS_ACTION, LATEST_ACTION (single, replaced), HAS_VERSION, HAS_AMENDMENT, HAS_POLICY_AREA, HAS_SUBJECT, RELATED_TO (directional, not symmetric). title: P1 Fix pending LLM counter leak + add device/model labels to RTF histogram
description: Two small correctness bugs in dagster_io metrics flagged by the ML systems engineer. (1) llm.py:93 and :126 increment LLM_REQUESTS{status=pending} at request start but never decrement — pending is effectively a monotonic counter of historical starts, not an in-flight gauge. Fix: drop the pending label emission entirely (success/error on completion is sufficient) OR replace with a proper LLM_REQUESTS_INFLIGHT Gauge labelled {model, operation} that is inc()'d in a try/finally. Prefer the gauge approach because it enables 'LLM saturation' alerts. (2) metrics.py:195 TRANSCRIPTION_REALTIME_FACTOR has only a 'backend' label, so the silent OpenVINO GPU to CPU fallback at transcription.py:110-114 is invisible in Grafana — both paths look identical. title: Audit audit-log payloads: replace inlined data with refs to persistent IDs
description:
The bench audit log (libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/bench/event_store.py — hive-partitioned parquet under bench-cache/events/doc_id=<doc>/) currently stores some events with full inlined data (e.g. chunk_extracted carries the full mentions[] array, pack_evidence completion carries kept_windows[] with offsets, possibly raw doc text in details). This bloats every parquet partition and inflates the per-doc events fetch (CD-niob) — a single chunk_extracted with 500 mentions is hundreds of KB even though that data already lives canonically in the silver layer (e.g. {family}_chunks, {family}_mentions, pack_evidence outputs).

Audit goal: for every node_name we emit, identify which fields in details inline data that already exists in a persistent datamodel (silver/gold parquet, GLiNER cache, pack outputs). Replace with reference IDs (chunk_id, mention_ids, window_id, doc_id) and rely on the SPA to fetch the canonical data on-demand via the docs/{id}/text + chunks endpoints already in viewer/routes/.

Steps:
1. Enumerate every event emitted by the pipeline. Grep for ctx.emit / event_store.append / EVENT_STORE.append in libs/dagster-io and packages/media-ingest/src — list (node_name, status, details schema).
2. For each event, classify each details field: (a) skinny meta — keep (counts, durations, status, refs); (b) large inlined — flag for conversion to reference (full text, full mentions list, kept_windows full payloads, raw extraction outputs).
3. For each flagged field, identify the canonical persistence (silver row, GLiNER chunk_extracted artifact in S3, pack output, etc.) and the existing/needed viewer-api endpoint to resolve the ref. Many already exist (docs/{id}/text, chunks, mentions, ner-encoder mentions).
4. Propose minimal-diff swap: change emitter to write the ref + a small preview/count, change consumer (StateInspector / DocumentSourcePanel / NerEncoderDetail / PackDetail) to fetch canonical data via existing useDocumentData / new per-domain hooks when the user actually drills in.
5. Measure before/after: avg event row size in parquet; total partition size for a typical 5k-event doc; per-doc events fetch payload (which CD-niob will be exercising).

Why now: dovetails with CD-niob (per-doc events fetch + React Query cache). Smaller events = faster cache fills, less S3 cost, less DuckDB scan time. Large inlined data also makes the audit log hard to diff between runs (semantic noise from float/UUID drift).

Out of scope:
- Removing or compressing the silver layer canonical data — only the audit-log copy.
- Backwards-compat shims for old runs — forward-only per project conventions; old runs render with whatever inlined data they have.
- Schema versioning of events — separate concern.

Deliverable: an inventory doc + a sequenced patch list (which event to slim first, in what order — probably highest-impact first: chunk_extracted mentions, pack_evidence kept_windows, then the long-tail).

title: Audit log events API: per-doc on-demand fetch (drop server-side aggregation)
description:
Today /viewer/api/bench/runs/{run_id}/events?limit= returns NDJSON aggregating events across ALL doc partitions in the run, server-capped at 50000. Symptoms (CD-ugfx QA verifier hit it): limit=80000 silently 422s; large runs bump the cap and clip events. Root: we aggregate hive partitions per request, expensive + unnecessary since the StateInspector only ever consumes events for ONE doc at a time. Proposed redesign — partition-aware fetch flow:

1. New cheap endpoint /runs/{run_id}/docs returning [{doc_id, event_count, has_chunks, has_consensus, has_pack, has_spo}, ...] populated from S3 partition listing (no event reads, just object metadata). Powers DocRailV2 sidebar without a full events fetch.
2. New per-doc endpoint /runs/{run_id}/docs/{doc_id}/events streaming the events for that single hive partition only. Already efficient (one parquet file).
3. Frontend (DocRailV2 + StateInspector + useRunStream): virtualized list; events fetched on doc selection (or prefetch on hover); cache per (runId, docId) with react-query.
4. Drop the 50000 cap once we are per-doc — single-doc events are bounded by the doc's own pipeline (~20-50k events worst case).

Why now: discovered while wiring QA verifier scripts that the existing aggregate endpoint clips on big runs and silently 422s above 50000. Also the SPA's whole-run fetch on every doc switch is wasted bandwidth — every partition is re-streamed even though only one matters.
design:
# Per-doc fetch + React Query cache integration

## Context
The current /viewer/api/bench/runs/{run_id}/events?limit=50000 endpoint aggregates every hive partition in the run, streamed via NDJSON. Two distinct problems converge on the same fix:

1. **Server-side aggregation pain (CD-niob original):** silent 422 above 50000, bandwidth waste re-streaming every partition on every doc switch, slow DocRail population because nothing about the run is summarisable without a full events fetch.
2. **Frontend cache pain (new — same patch):** `useRunStream.ts` hand-rolls a 3s setTimeout poll over the aggregate endpoint with no cache. Switching tabs (StateInspector → BenchmarkReport → back) re-pays the full 50k-event fetch even though parquet from a completed run is immutable. `useRuns.ts` has the same shape.

Both problems vanish with the same redesign: split the API per-doc, then key React Query queries on (runId, docId). Each query is small, cacheable, and immutable once the run completes.

---

## Backend changes

### `GET /viewer/api/bench/runs/{run_id}/docs`  (new, cheap)
Returns `[{doc_id, event_count, has_chunks, has_consensus, has_pack, has_spo}, ...]` populated by S3 partition listing only — no parquet reads, just object metadata + a per-partition COUNT(*) (DuckDB push-down on the hive partition stat). Powers DocRailV2 sidebar without a full events fetch. Sub-100ms response on a 50-doc run.

### `GET /viewer/api/bench/runs/{run_id}/docs/{doc_id}/events`  (new, on-demand)
Streams NDJSON for a single hive partition. Already efficient — one parquet file. **No `limit` param needed**: single-doc events are bounded by the pipeline (~5-50k events worst case for a long video). Drop the 50000 cap entirely.

### `GET /viewer/api/bench/runs/{run_id}/events?limit=N`  (existing, deprecate)
Keep for one release (BenchmarkReport's run-level F1 strip still uses it via `useRunReport` — that flow already works through `report.json` though, so verify before deletion). Mark with deprecation header; remove once StateInspector + DocRailV2 are migrated.

### `GET /viewer/api/bench/runs`  (existing, no change)
Returns `{runs[], latest, live}`. Still the source of truth for the run-picker.

Files: `packages/media-ingest/src/media_ingest/viewer/routes/bench.py`, `services/bench_event_store.py`.

---

## Frontend changes — React Query migration

### `hooks/queryKeys.ts`  (new)
Central key registry so invalidation is predictable:
```ts
export const qk = {
  bench: {
    runs: () => ["bench", "runs"] as const,
    docs: (runId: string | null) => ["bench", "docs", runId] as const,
    docEvents: (runId: string | null, docId: string | null) =>
      ["bench", "events", runId, docId] as const,
    report: (runId: string | null) => ["bench", "report", runId] as const,
    groundTruthActive: () => ["bench", "ground-truth", "active"] as const,
  },
};
```

### `hooks/useRuns.ts`  →  `useQuery`
```ts
useQuery<RunsListing>({
  queryKey: qk.bench.runs(),
  queryFn: fetchRuns,
  staleTime: 10_000,
  refetchInterval: 30_000,
  refetchIntervalInBackground: false,
  refetchOnWindowFocus: false,
  placeholderData: { runs: [], latest: null, live: null },
});
```

### `hooks/useRunDocs.ts`  (new)
```ts
useQuery({
  queryKey: qk.bench.docs(runId),
  queryFn: () => fetchDocs(runId!),
  enabled: !!runId,
  staleTime: isLiveRun ? 5_000 : Infinity,   // partition list grows during a live run
  refetchInterval: isLiveRun ? 5_000 : false,
  refetchIntervalInBackground: false,
  gcTime: 30 * 60_000,
});
```

### `hooks/useRunStream.ts`  →  per-doc `useQuery` (the big one)
```ts
const { data: runs } = useRuns();
const targetRunId = pinnedRunId ?? runs?.latest ?? null;
const isLive = targetRunId !== null && targetRunId === runs?.live;

const query = useQuery<RunEvent[]>({
  queryKey: qk.bench.docEvents(targetRunId, selectedDocId),
  enabled: !!targetRunId && !!selectedDocId,
  queryFn: () => fetchDocEvents(targetRunId!, selectedDocId!),

  // Live partition: poll fast, never trust the cache.
  // Historical partition: parquet is immutable → cache forever.
  staleTime: isLive ? 0 : Infinity,
  refetchInterval: isLive ? 3_000 : false,

  refetchIntervalInBackground: false,  // pause when tab hidden
  refetchOnWindowFocus: false,          // live polling already covers it

  // 30 min gcTime: tab-switching back to a recently-viewed run/doc is
  // free. Long enough to make navigation feel instant; short enough that
  // abandoned runs flush eventually. (Default 5min is too short for the
  // 5-50k-event payload.)
  gcTime: 30 * 60_000,

  // Smooth doc-picker transitions: keep showing previous events while
  // new doc loads — avoids empty-state flash.
  placeholderData: (prev) => prev,
});
```

### Live → completed transition
When `runs.live` flips from `<runId>` → null, fire one final invalidate so the cache picks up the consolidated parquet (per CD-jzkg Phase 4 the per-doc consolidate happens at run-end):
```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (prevLive === targetRunId && runs?.live !== targetRunId) {
    qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: qk.bench.docs(targetRunId) });
    qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["bench", "events", targetRunId] }); // all docs
  }
}, [runs?.live]);
```

### Cache-setting summary

| Setting | Live run + doc | Historical run + doc | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| staleTime | 0 | Infinity | Live parquet is being written; historical is immutable. |
| refetchInterval | 3_000 | false | Match today's 3s tick for live; no point polling immutable data. |
| refetchIntervalInBackground | false | false | Don't burn bandwidth tab-hidden. |
| gcTime | 30 * 60_000 | 30 * 60_000 | Cross-tab/run/doc switches feel free; abandoned data still flushes. |
| placeholderData: prev | yes | yes | No empty-state flash when doc/run changes. |
| refetchOnWindowFocus | false | false | Live already polls; historical immutable. |

---

## DocRailV2 + StateInspector wiring

- DocRailV2 calls `useRunDocs(runId)` (cheap) for the sidebar list — no events fetched until selection.
- StateInspector reads selectedDocId from URL (`?doc=<id>`) and passes to `useRunStream(runId, docId)`.
- Optional: prefetch on hover via `qc.prefetchQuery({ queryKey: qk.bench.docEvents(runId, hoveredDocId), ... })` — react-query wires this in 5 lines.
- Virtualize the DocRailV2 list (already on `@tanstack/react-virtual` per package.json) once docs/run can return 100+ entries.

---

## Critical files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/media-ingest/src/media_ingest/viewer/routes/bench.py` | New `/runs/{id}/docs` endpoint + `/runs/{id}/docs/{doc_id}/events` endpoint. Deprecate the aggregate `/events` (keep one release). |
| `packages/media-ingest/src/media_ingest/viewer/services/bench_event_store.py` | Add `list_run_docs(run_id) -> [DocSummary]` (S3 partition listing + COUNT). Add `read_doc_events(run_id, doc_id) -> Iterator[RunEvent]` for the new endpoint. |
| `viewer-ui/src/hooks/queryKeys.ts` | New — central key registry. |
| `viewer-ui/src/hooks/useRuns.ts` | Replace setTimeout polling with `useQuery`. |
| `viewer-ui/src/hooks/useRunDocs.ts` | New — wraps `/runs/{id}/docs`. |
| `viewer-ui/src/hooks/useRunStream.ts` | Replace setTimeout polling with `useQuery`; key on (runId, docId); live/historical staleTime split. |
| `viewer-ui/src/hooks/useRunReport.ts` | Re-key via `qk.bench.report` for consistency. |
| `viewer-ui/src/components/state/DocRailV2.tsx` | Consume `useRunDocs` instead of deriving from full events array. |
| `viewer-ui/src/pages/StateInspector.tsx` | Pass `selectedDocId` into `useRunStream`. |

Reuse, don't reinvent: `QueryClient` + `QueryClientProvider` already mounted (`App.tsx:15-22`). `useRunReport` (`hooks/useRunReport.ts`) is the existing pattern reference for "long staleTime + 404-tolerant". `console.log("[audit-log] reader=duckdb …")` line in `useRunStream.ts` stays — useful for spotting cache hits vs refetches.

---

## Verification

1. **Cold load StateInspector with `?run=<historical>&doc=<id>`:** network tab shows ONE `/docs/<id>/events`. Switch to BenchmarkReport, switch back — no second request. (Cache hit.)
2. **Live run polling:** start a bench, watch `/docs/<active>/events` fire every 3s. Tab away — polling stops within 3s. Tab back — resumes.
3. **Run completion:** when `runs.live` flips to null, observe one final `/docs` + `/events` invalidate, then quiesce.
4. **Doc-picker switch within a cached run:** flicking between two docs in DocRailV2 is instant (cache hit). React Query Devtools shows two cached entries with `staleTime: Infinity`.
5. **Memory:** load 5 historical runs/docs, navigate away, wait 30 min, return — only the most-recently-viewed remains.
6. **Limit removed:** verify a synthetic 80k-event single-doc partition loads end-to-end with no 422.
7. **Lint/types:** `yarn typecheck && yarn lint` green; backend `ruff check` green.
8. **No e2e regressions:** `yarn test:e2e` (Playwright) — StateInspector smoke spec still passes.

---

## Non-goals

- Optimistic updates / mutations — events are read-only from the UI.
- Persisted cache (`@tanstack/react-query-persist-client`) — dev-only, no need to survive page reloads.
- Cursor / pagination on per-doc events — single-doc bounded by pipeline; revisit only if a doc exceeds ~100k events.
- Migrating `useDocumentData` / `useAnnotations` / `useSpeakerNames` — already react-query, scoped per-doc, settings appropriate.
notes:
Plan integrates two simultaneous concerns: (1) original CD-niob — per-doc partition fetch on the backend (drops server-side aggregation, removes the 50000 cap, fixes silent 422s); and (2) frontend — migrate useRunStream + useRuns from hand-rolled setTimeout polling to @tanstack/react-query with run-status-aware cache settings. Both share the same key insight: per-doc immutable parquet → per-(runId, docId) query key → staleTime: Infinity for historical, 3s polling for live. See design field for full plan + cache-setting rationale + file list. Recommend doing as one integrated PR since the per-doc API shape determines the React Query key structure.

Related: CD-kpb6 audits audit-log event payloads for inlined large data (full text, full mentions[], kept_windows[]) that should reference persistent IDs instead. Slimming events first makes the per-doc fetch even cheaper and shrinks the parquet partitions CD-niob is targeting. Can run in parallel; CD-kpb6 produces an inventory + sequenced slim-down patches that don't depend on the API split.

title: DocumentSourcePanel shows truncated doc text (capped at 4 KiB by event_tail.emit_chunk_text)
description:
DocumentSourcePanel.tsx pulls full doc text from the longest `{doc_id}:_ner_<enc>` chunk_loaded event, but those events are capped at max_chars=4096 by event_tail.emit_chunk_text (libs/dagster-io/.../bench/event_tail.py). For congress bills this shows ~4 KiB of a 500+ KiB document — the chunk-marker overlay is meaningless because it only sees the first ~6% of the doc.

Fix options:
1. Lift the cap for :_ner_<enc> emits specifically (those are doc-scoped, not chunk-scoped — the 4 KiB limit was a per-chunk size budget). One-line change at the emit site in ner_ensemble.py.
2. Stream the full doc from the silver layer on demand via a viewer-api endpoint /viewer/api/silver/<doc_id>/text. Scales better but more plumbing.
3. Keep the cap but mark truncation in DocumentSourcePanel + render a 'show full doc' button that fetches from S3.

Recommend (1) for now: the bench's events.jsonl is already a few MB; pulling 4× more for the per-encoder doc text isn't a real cost. If it becomes one, escalate to (2).

Acceptance: open StateInspector for congress-bill-hr5376-117 (~580k chars). DocumentSourcePanel shows the full doc text scrollable; chunk markers cover the entire range, not just the first page.
notes:
Design (revised 2026-05-04, supersedes 'lift the cap'):

Don't inline doc text in chunk_loaded events at all. Emit a URI
reference to the silver-layer asset that already holds the canonical
text; viewer-api streams it on demand when DocumentSourcePanel opens.

Wire:
1. event_store.emit_chunk_text becomes emit_chunk_loaded(chunk_id, *,
   doc_id, char_count, silver_uri, domain, ...) — same idempotency,
   but details now carries silver_uri instead of text.
2. New viewer-api route GET /viewer/api/docs/<doc_id>/text that:
   a. Resolves silver_uri from the most recent chunk_loaded event for
      that doc OR from a per-domain default path (the asset key →
      silver path mapping is already deterministic).
   b. Reads the parquet/JSONL, concatenates the raw text in chunk_index
      order, returns text/plain.
   c. Caches by (run_id, doc_id) in-process for the FastAPI worker.
3. DocumentSourcePanel calls the new endpoint on doc selection (one
   fetch per doc, results cached client-side via tanstack-query).

What stays inline: chunk_extracted.details.mentions / propositions —
those are the pipeline's *output*, not the input, and are smaller per
event. Externalizing them would mean fetching from S3 to render the
detail panels, which is more user-facing latency for marginal payload
savings.

Acceptance:
- chunk_loaded events on a 580 KiB congress bill run carry no inline
  text in details (just silver_uri + char_count + chunk_index).
- DocumentSourcePanel renders the *full* doc with chunk markers
  spanning the whole range, not just the first 4 KiB.
- events.jsonl size drops by >50% on a full-corpus run vs the inline
  baseline.
- Old runs with inline text still render (DocumentSourcePanel falls
  back to details.text when silver_uri is absent).

title: Media-ingest entities flow through pipeline as canonical_type=UNKNOWN
description:
Latest full-corpus bench (2026-05-04-185418): 5,912 entities show with consensus_type='UNKNOWN' in the report, all media-ingest. Congress (15 entities, ORG/LAW/PERSON) and leaks (31 entities, OTHER) type correctly.

Two related root causes (the symptom is the same — entities reach consensus but with no canonical type):

A. Domain mislabel: media-ingest chunks in the current silver layer were chunked BEFORE commit 6ef1293 added `domain=media_ingest` to the metadata. So domain=None → falls to 'unknown' bucket. Fix: re-run `task seed:media` (or the equivalent chunks-regen task) to backfill silver.

B. Even after the domain fix, why is mention_type='UNKNOWN' for media chunks? Hypothesis: media chunks contain primarily transcript text where speaker turns were removed (the recent inline_speaker_tags=False default flip in commit 4f91a60). Encoders then see uninterrupted speech with no clear named entities → emit OTHER labels which canonicalize to 'OTHER' (consensus_taxonomy.py: gliner-pii now restricted to PII canonicals; everyone else passes through as canonical-string). But 'UNKNOWN' specifically isn't in any TYPE_CANONICAL map — so something else is setting that literal.

Investigate: pull the per-encoder mention list for one media doc and look at what the encoders actually emitted as mention_type:
  mise exec -- python -c "
  from dagster_io.bench import S3BenchmarkStore
  s = S3BenchmarkStore()
  ext = s.client.get_object('bench/runs/2026-05-04-185418/extractions/extraction_gliner-medium.json')
  import json; d = json.loads(ext)
  media_mentions = [m for m in d.get('mentions', []) if 'show' in (m.get('chunk_id', '') or '') or '4-9-26' in (m.get('document_id', '') or '')]
  print('media mentions:', len(media_mentions))
  for m in media_mentions[:10]: print(m.get('text'), '·', m.get('mention_type'), '·', m.get('document_id'))
  "

Acceptance:
- After re-chunking media: domain breakdown shows 'media: <N>' instead of 'unknown: <N>'.
- Per-encoder mention output for media docs has mention_type ∈ {PERSON, ORG, GPE, …}, not 'UNKNOWN'.
- Consensus output for media docs has canonical_type ∈ MentionType enum values, not the literal 'UNKNOWN'.

title: Hive-style doc_id partitioning for the bench audit log (Phase 4)
description:
Phase 4 of CD-jzkg. Phases 1-3 shipped a single events.parquet per run; expected scale (300k-1M events/run on full bench) means viewer queries that filter by doc_id should partition-prune to a single file rather than scan the whole run.

## Goal
Write hive-partitioned parquet under each run dir:

  s3://dagster/bench/runs/<run_id>/events/
    doc_id=<doc_id>/data.parquet
    doc_id=__run__/data.parquet   (harness-level events with no doc_id)

DuckDB auto-prunes via read_parquet('events/**/*.parquet', hive_partitioning=true) — viewer endpoint code stays the same, just gets faster.

## Why doc_id specifically
StateInspector + AuditViewer + ChunkRail all scope to a single doc. Partition by the dominant filter axis. Model would over-shard (15×1000 = 15k tiny files), source has too-uneven cardinality, run_id is already the directory.

## Scope
1. BenchEventStore: re-key per-process buffers from (writer_pid,) to (writer_pid, doc_id). Flush each (pid, doc_id) bucket to its own shard file.
2. Consolidation: at run-end, COPY each doc_id group into events/doc_id=<doc>/data.parquet. Drop the per-pid shards.
3. /events endpoint: hive_partitioning=true on read. Existing ?doc_id= facet now triggers pruning automatically.
4. Backwards compat: read path accepts BOTH legacy events.parquet AND the new partitioned layout via read_parquet(..., union_by_name=true). Old runs keep working untouched — forward-only for new writes.
5. Tilt buttons (stats/errors/schema/tail/runs-s3): update the TARGET resolution to handle the new layout. The 'duck' shell wrapper just passes globs to read_parquet so most should work as-is.
6. Tests: parity test gone (Phase 3 deleted it). Add a unit test asserting (a) writes land in correct partition, (b) hive read with doc_id filter only opens 1 file, (c) cross-doc query reads all partitions, (d) backward-compat with legacy single-file layout.

## Out of scope
- Multi-writer-per-doc coordination (still one writer per doc; multiple writers across docs OK).
- Iceberg / DuckLake migration — keep it plain hive parquet for now.

## Estimated work
~1 day. Smaller than Phases 1-3 because read path mostly unchanged.

title: DuckDB-backed bench audit log (alongside jsonl, strangler fig)
description:
Replace the current events.jsonl approach for bench audit logs with a DuckDB-backed store, implemented alongside the jsonl path (no feature flag) so we can validate parity in real runs before strangler-figging the old path out.

## Why
Current events.jsonl + S3 upload doesn't scale to a swarm of concurrent exgraphs:
- Concurrent writers need file locking, easy to corrupt
- Filtering is O(N) — every viewer query rescans the file
- Cross-run analysis means joining N jsonl files manually
- Polling-as-live doesn't scale to many sessions

## Approach
DuckDB in-process columnar store. Single bench.duckdb file (or memory-mapped from S3 via httpfs). Native parquet I/O so archival is smaller + faster than jsonl. SQL frontend for the viewer's audit + state-inspector pages instead of in-JS filtering.

## Strangler-fig phases (per user direction)
1. Dual-write: harness writes BOTH events.jsonl (existing) AND duckdb (new), no flag, no behavior change for viewers.
2. Dual-read: viewer queries duckdb, falls back to jsonl on miss. Compare results; ensure parity over a real bench.
3. Strangle: drop jsonl writes, jsonl SSE shim, jsonl S3 upload. AuditViewer + StateInspector exclusively duckdb-backed.

## Deliverables
- BenchEventStore in libs/dagster-io with append(event) + query(sql) backed by DuckDB
- Schema design (events table — ts, run_id, source, node_name, status, model, doc_id, chunk_id, retry_count, code_location, state JSON, details JSON, indexes)
- Concurrency model for swarm-of-exgraphs writers (per-process parquet shards merged at run-end vs shared duckdb instance)
- Viewer endpoint that takes SQL filters: /viewer/api/bench/runs/<id>/events?where=...
- Migration plan + tests: parity test asserting jsonl-derived events == duckdb query results across a real run

## Out of scope
- Replacing the run-bus (already removed in 0adacd9)
- Replacing the bench S3 store altogether — only the events log changes
notes: Phase 1 (dual-write) shipped in ac90c2b. Parity test green on real bench run (109 events identical between events.jsonl and events.parquet, --ensemble-only --ensemble gliner-medium). Phase 2 (viewer dual-read) and Phase 3 (strangle) follow.

Currently report.py:51-56 tags model_type='llm' for any model lacking 'encoder' or 'extraction-specialist' tags, and useModelGrouping.ts groups by m.type returning 'llm' (or by tier returning 'tier2' which has a slot in GROUP_SORT_ORDER). title: nuextract-2.0-8b → Ollama HTTP 500 on full-corpus bench
description: During the full-corpus bench run (5 NER encoders + 3 SPO LLMs across all local docs), nuextract-2.0-8b raised `httpx.HTTPStatusError: Server error '500 Internal Server Error' for url 'http://localhost:11434/api/chat'` from `catalyst_langgraph.clients.nuextract._call_llm` (line 168). Other 4 encoders unaffected. Hypotheses: (a) context-length overflow on a long chunk, (b) Ollama daemon hiccup under concurrent load (5 NER + 3 SPO simultaneously), (c) a specific bad input the model crashes on. Need: per-call retry logic in nuextract client, OR a graceful skip+log so a single chunk failure doesn't blank the encoder's row.
notes:
Concrete retry design (post-discussion 2026-05-04):

Wrap _call_llm in nuextract.py + universalner.py with an exponential
backoff retry decorator. Retry policy:
- Retryable: HTTPStatusError where response.status_code in {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}; httpx.ReadTimeout, ConnectError, RemoteProtocolError, RemoteProtocolError, ReadError
- NOT retryable: 4xx besides 408/429 (re-fails); JSON parse errors (logic bug, not transient)
- 3 attempts, base 1.0s, cap 30s, full jitter (random.uniform(0, base * 2**attempt))
- Log each retry via logger.warning("[nuextract] retry %d/3 after %s: %s", ...)
  so the TUI surfaces it
- Single shared decorator in libs/catalyst-langgraph-aio/src/catalyst_langgraph/clients/_retry.py
  applied to all 4 raise_for_status sites

Use stdlib only (no tenacity dep) — async generator for sleep timing.
Smoke test: monkeypatch the httpx.AsyncClient.post to fail with 500 twice
then succeed; assert the call returns and warning logs fire.

title: EPIC: ClusterCache → @multi_asset migration (ner_mentions + entity_clusters as Dagster assets)
description:
Replace the hand-rolled `ClusterCache` with proper Dagster `@multi_asset` definitions per code location. Each domain emits two partitioned silver assets:

```
media_chunks (silver, exists today)
   └── ner_pass (multi_asset, NEW)
         ├── media_ner_mentions  (silver, partitioned by doc_id)
         └── media_entity_clusters (silver, partitioned by doc_id)
              └── (consumed by bench harness via materialize() + IO manager read)
```

Same pattern for `congress_data` and `open_leaks`.

**Why** (vs the current hand-rolled `dagster_io.cluster_cache.ClusterCache`):

1. **No parallel ETL.** Today the bench harness has its own cache (with its own schema versioning, its own backward-compat path). Dagster already provides exactly this for typed asset materialisation — we shouldn't be reinventing it.

2. **Free dependency tracking.** Change the NER reference model → Dagster invalidates the partitions automatically. Today we hand-roll cache keys via `sha256(doc + ner_model + params)`.

3. **Free observability.** Asset graph in the Dagster UI shows ner_mentions/entity_clusters alongside chunks/embeddings. Materialisation history, lineage, run metadata all light up.

4. **Solves the warm-cache mention bug structurally.** Today CD-jsha persists mentions alongside clusters in the cache to handle warm hits. With assets, the IO manager handles persistence — there's nothing to reinvent.

5. **Aligns with existing pattern.** `media_chunks`, `media_embeddings` are already Dagster assets. ner_pass should join them.

**Scope:** Decompose into phases (sub-issues spawned separately when this epic kicks off):

- **Phase A — Asset definitions** (per code location): write `@multi_asset` `ner_pass` for media_ingest, congress_data, open_leaks. Same shape across all three; lift shared logic into a helper.
- **Phase B — Bench harness rewire**: replace `_phase_a_build_cluster_cache` with `materialize_to_memory(...)` (or `materialize` + read-back via IO manager). Drop `ClusterCache` entirely. Drop the `_run_ner_and_cluster` helper. Drop the `shared_mentions: dict` param threading on `extract_with_shared_clusters` since assets carry their own data.
- **Phase C — Cleanup**: delete `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/cluster_cache.py`, `libs/dagster-io/tests/test_cluster_cache.py`, the CD-jsha compat code. Update viewer references if any.
- **Phase D — Verification**: smoke run end-to-end on the new path; confirm bench results match the pre-migration baseline; confirm StateInspector still groups events correctly.

**Prerequisites:** Phase 4 of v3 (CD-yebc, GT regen + bench validation) should land first so we have a stable baseline to compare migration outcomes against.</description>
<design>**Multi-asset shape:**

```python
# packages/media-ingest/src/media_ingest/assets/ner_pass.py (new)
from dagster import multi_asset, AssetOut, AssetIn, Output, AssetExecutionContext

@multi_asset(
    partitions_def=media_partitions,
    outs={
        "media_ner_mentions":    AssetOut(io_manager_key="optional_io_manager", group_name="media_ingest"),
        "media_entity_clusters": AssetOut(io_manager_key="optional_io_manager", group_name="media_ingest"),
    },
    ins={"chunks": AssetIn("media_chunks")},
    description="NER + entity clustering pass (shared across all extraction models in v3 entity-anchored topology)",
    compute_kind="ml",
)
def media_ner_pass(
    context: AssetExecutionContext,
    embeddings: EmbeddingResource,
    chunks: list[TextChunk],
) -> tuple[Output[list[dict]], Output[list[dict]]]:
    from dagster_io.extraction import _build_pipelines, _group_chunks_into_docs
    docs = _group_chunks_into_docs(chunks)
    if not docs:
        return Output([], output_name="media_ner_mentions"), Output([], output_name="media_entity_clusters")
    
    # Single doc per partition — group should yield exactly 1
    doc = docs[0]
    ner_pipeline, _spo, _client, _emb = _build_pipelines()
    ner_state_input = {...}
    ner_result = await ner_pipeline.ainvoke(ner_state_input)
    
    return (
        Output((ner_result.get("stages") or {}).get("ner", {}).get("accepted") or [], output_name="media_ner_mentions"),
        Output(ner_result.get("entity_clusters") or [], output_name="media_entity_clusters"),
    )
```

**Bench harness rewire** (sketch):

```python
def _phase_a_materialize_assets(docs):
    """Materialize ner_mentions + entity_clusters across all 3 code locations
    for the given partition keys. Returns dicts keyed by doc_id."""
    from dagster import materialize_to_memory
    
    result = materialize_to_memory(
        assets=[media_ner_mentions, media_entity_clusters, congress_ner_mentions, ...],
        partition_key=...,
        resources={...},
    )
    return _read_outputs_from_result(result)
```

**Avoid pitfalls** (from prior session memories):
- IO manager wiring is touchy — test that `OptionalMinioIOManager` correctly persists `list[dict]` outputs. The shape needs to round-trip through whatever serializer the IO manager uses (pickle vs JSON vs parquet — match what `media_embeddings` uses).
- Ensure `EmbeddingResource` is correctly resolved per the v3 + CD-27ba EnvVar wiring.
- DAGSTER_CODE_LOCATION must be set per-domain when materializing across code locations from the bench harness.</design>
<acceptance>1. Three `@multi_asset` definitions: `media_ner_pass`, `congress_ner_pass`, `leaks_ner_pass`. Each emits its `*_ner_mentions` + `*_entity_clusters` partitioned by doc_id.
2. Bench harness `_phase_a_*` uses `materialize_to_memory` (or equivalent) instead of `ClusterCache`.
3. `dagster_io/cluster_cache.py` and its tests deleted. The CD-jsha schema fix becomes obsolete.
4. Bench end-to-end smoke run produces the same mention + SPO counts as the pre-migration run on the same corpus.
5. Dagster asset graph shows the new assets as siblings of `media_chunks` / `media_embeddings`.
6. StateInspector + viewer continue to work (events.jsonl shape unchanged).
7. Closes CD-jsha as obsolete (its compat code is deleted, its tests are deleted).</acceptance>

title: Phase 4: GT regen + bench validation on v3 topology
description:
**Parent epic**: CD-rwlq.

Regenerate ground-truth corpus on the v3 entity-anchored topology. Verify scoring matches expected ranges. Validate the epic acceptance criteria end-to-end.

**Workflow:**
1. Run a full bench cycle with the new topology against existing GT (which is now span-anchored from Phase 0). Initial scoring will be informative but not directly comparable to old scores because the SPO call distribution is fundamentally different.
2. Use the ensemble GT generator (`scripts/sample_gt_candidates.py` + the SPA's GroundTruthPanel) to produce fresh GT entries on the v3 evidence windows. Reviewer pass: ~6 hours of human attention.
3. Score v3 model output against v3 GT. Document the new baseline metrics in `BENCHMARK.md`.
4. Compare per-domain: which models improved, which regressed. Flag any unexpected drops for triage.

**Files affected:**
- `BENCHMARK.md` — update with new baseline metrics, note the topology change
- `docs/EXTRACTION-MODEL-RESEARCH.md` — append a section comparing v2 (linear) vs v3 (entity-anchored) outcomes
- Possibly `tests/benchmark_config.py` — re-tune any per-model thresholds that shifted</description>
<design>**Validation matrix** (per the epic acceptance):

| Check | Method | Pass criterion |
|---|---|---|
| Wikileaks cable masthead produces ≥1 prop | StateInspector cable doc, evidence-window view | At least one window has prop count > 0 |
| Joe-rogan greeting chunks → 0 windows | StateInspector media doc | Header chunk produces 0 evidence windows |
| SPO calls drop to ~1/3 | Compare `events.jsonl` extract_spo count v2 vs v3 | <0.4 ratio (v3/v2) |
| GT scoring works on new topology | Run scoring on v3 output + v3 GT | precision/recall in plausible ranges |
| Per-model bench produces fixtures | `task bench:run -- --models <all>` | All 7 models produce non-empty extraction.json |

**GT regen process:**
1. Pick 5 representative docs spanning all 3 domains (media, congress, leaks).
2. Run v3 extraction across the full ensemble (gliner-large, gliner-pii, nuextract-2.0, gemma3-12b).
3. Use ensemble GT sampler to produce candidate annotations.
4. Manual review pass — accept/reject candidates per evidence window.
5. Save as new GT files in span-anchored format.
6. Spot-check: 2-3 windows from each domain manually inspected for "did we get the right propositions for this evidence?"

**Out of scope for this phase:**
- Re-tuning any bench config thresholds (do that as follow-up if metrics look off).

title: Phase 3: Per-model window sizing — MODEL_WINDOWS registry + bench harness rewire
description:
**Parent epic**: CD-rwlq.

Add `MODEL_WINDOWS` registry; `pack_evidence` packs per `model_name`. Bench harness re-chunks per-model (cheap pack step) from a single Qwen3-8B embedding cache (expensive).

**Files affected:**
- `libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/chunking.py` — add `MODEL_WINDOWS` dict
- `tests/benchmark_harness.py` — load doc texts, pre-compute entity clusters once per doc, re-pack per model
- `tests/shared/medallion.py` — add `load_doc_texts()` helper alongside existing `load_chunks()`</description>
<design>**Registry** (`chunking.py`):
```python
MODEL_WINDOWS: dict[str, int] = {
    "gliner-medium":   320,    # 384 cap minus 32 overlap budget
    "gliner-large":    320,
    "gliner-pii":      320,
    "nuextract-1.5":   3500,   # 4K context, leave room for prompt
    "nuextract-2.0-8b": 7500,  # 8K
    "universalner-7b": 7500,
    "gemma3-12b":      24000,
    "gpt-4o-mini":     8000,
    "claude-haiku":    16000,
}

def window_for_model(name: str) -> int:
    if name in MODEL_WINDOWS:
        return MODEL_WINDOWS[name]
    # Heuristic fallback by name pattern
    if "gliner" in name.lower(): return 320
    if "gemma" in name.lower() or "claude" in name.lower(): return 16000
    return 4000  # safe default
```

**Bench harness flow** (`tests/benchmark_harness.py::_run_model`):
```python
# Phase A — once per doc, model-independent (cached):
doc_texts = load_doc_texts(sample_per_domain=N)
for doc in doc_texts:
    ner_mentions = await ner_pipeline.ainvoke(doc)  # cached by doc hash
    clusters = cluster_entities(ner_mentions, embedder=qwen3_resource)  # cached
    # store clusters keyed by doc.id

# Phase B — per (doc, model):
for cfg in models:
    set_env(cfg)
    for doc, clusters in cached:
        windows = pack_evidence(clusters, model_name=cfg.name)  # cheap, no cache needed
        for w in windows:
            spo_result = await spo_pipeline.ainvoke(w)
            accumulate(spo_result)
    save_extraction(cfg.name, fixture)
```

**Cache key for clusters** (in addition to embedding cache from Phase 1):
- Key: `sha256(doc.text + ner_model_name + cluster_threshold)`
- Path: `s3://dagster/silver/<code_loc>/cluster_cache/<key>.json`
- Skips both NER + cluster on rerun for the same NER model.

**Tests:**
1. `test_model_windows_registry.py`: lookup gliner → 320, gemma3 → 24000, unknown encoder → fallback.
2. `test_pack_per_model.py`: same cluster set produces different window counts for gliner vs gemma3.
3. `test_bench_harness_cache_hit.py`: second run of same fixture is faster than first (cache warm).</design>
<acceptance>1. `MODEL_WINDOWS` registry covers the 7 bench models with correct token counts.
2. `pack_evidence` produces different window counts for different models on the same cluster set (verified in unit test).
3. Bench harness re-chunks per-model from cached clusters; second run materially faster than first.
4. Bench `task bench:run` produces per-model fixtures with the new flow.
5. No regression in extraction counts for models running their native window size.</acceptance>
<labels>["chunking", "bench", "v3", "phase-3"]</labels>
</invoke>

title: Replace Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N] with a single repo-root resolver
description:
The pattern Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N] is scattered across the codebase — brittle (reordering directory depth breaks every call site silently), hard to reason about (developer counts directory hops in their head), and bug-prone (we already shipped one wrong count in libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/bench_store.py during the S3BenchmarkStore work).

Replace with a single source-of-truth resolver. Two reasonable shapes:

(a) Env-driven: CATALYST_REPO_ROOT env var set by Taskfile/Tiltfile/conftest, fall back to a single helper that walks up from a known marker file (pyproject.toml or .git). Pro: explicit; Con: more env-var sprawl.

(b) Helper function in dagster_io: e.g. dagster_io.paths.repo_root() walks up from __file__ looking for a sentinel (catalyst_repo.yaml or pyproject.toml at the repo root). Cached to avoid filesystem walks. Pro: zero config; Con: dependency cycle risk if anything in dagster_io.paths imports from elsewhere.

LEAN: option (b). One function, dagster_io.paths.repo_root(), walks up from __file__ until it finds 'catalyst_repo.yaml'. Replaces ~15 call sites that use parents[N] arithmetic.

Acceptance:
1. New module libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/paths.py with repo_root() (cached) + maybe test_output_root() (reads TEST_OUTPUT_ROOT env, defaults to repo_root() / '.test-output')
2. grep for 'parents\[' across libs/, packages/, tests/ → all call sites either use the helper or have a documented reason not to
3. bench_store.py, semantic_seed.py, harness, conftest.py all migrated
4. Forward-only: don't keep the parents[N] versions side-by-side.

title: pgvector: chunk_seeds table for SemanticChunkingSeed persistence
description:
Add chunk_seeds table to postgres-knowledge so per-chunk SemanticChunkingSeed records (chunk_id, domain, embedding, embedding_model, embedding_dimensions, char_count, semantic_hash, text_hash, created_at) are queryable via SQL alongside canonical_entities and speaker_profiles. The deterministic GT-candidate sampler (scripts/sample_gt_candidates.py) reads from chunk_seeds via SQL filter+ORDER BY embedding<=>:query_vec instead of recomputing vectors per run.

Schema sketch:
  CREATE TABLE chunk_seeds (
    chunk_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    domain TEXT NOT NULL,
    embedding vector(768) NOT NULL,
    embedding_model TEXT NOT NULL,
    embedding_dimensions INT NOT NULL,
    char_count INT NOT NULL,

    code_location TEXT,

  CREATE INDEX idx_chunk_seeds_embedding ON chunk_seeds USING ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops);
  CREATE INDEX idx_chunk_seeds_domain ON chunk_seeds (domain);

title: Research embedding model for SemanticChunkingSeed
description: Pick the embedding model that backs the per-asset SemanticChunkingSeed used to drive deterministic seed sampling across the live corpus. Requirements: (1) cheap to recompute on every text-asset materialization, (2) good cross-domain semantic diversity (media transcripts, congressional bills, leak cables), (3) stable to model upgrades — same hash class for similar text, (4) usable both in-cluster (CPU box, no GPU) and locally. Compare: text-embedding-3-small (current prod default per dagster_io.embedding_config), all-mpnet-base-v2 (local CPU, no API), bge-small-en-v1.5, jina-embeddings-v3, nomic-embed-text. Output: ADR + winning model wired into SemanticChunkingSeed dataclass.
notes:
STORAGE DECISION (2026-05-01): pgvector is the consolidated vector DB across catalyst-data. Already deployed — k8s/platform/postgres-knowledge.yaml runs pgvector/pgvector:pg16 with vector extension enabled. Live tables: canonical_entities.embedding vector(768), speaker_profiles.centroid vector(192), both indexed via ivfflat cosine. SemanticChunkingSeed adds a sibling table chunk_seeds in the same DB so all vectors live together and cross-table similarity joins are free SQL.

EMBEDDING MODEL — recommendation: pick a 768-dim model so chunk_seeds and canonical_entities share dimensionality. Top candidates at 768d: (a) nomic-embed-text (MIT license, 8192 ctx, strong cross-domain, runs on CPU — dev parity with cluster), (b) all-mpnet-base-v2 (proven, broad community, 384 ctx — too short for our chunks). text-embedding-3-small is 1536d so it forces a different vector column dimension, breaking the unified-table goal.

LEAN: nomic-embed-text @ 768d. Validates: dev runs CPU-only, cluster has same model via the LLM proxy, dimension matches canonical_entities for future cross-vector joins (chunk → canonical_entity similarity).

title: Wire congress_chunks asset to use XML-smart bill_chunker for bill documents
description:
Today congress-data has TWO chunker paths and they disagree:

1. packages/congress-data/src/congress_data/assets/chunks.py — congress_chunks asset (line 64) calls generic chunking.chunk_document(...) which uses RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter. Used by ALL congress document types including bills.

2. packages/congress-data/src/congress_data/assets/bill_tail.py — calls chunk_bill_text() from bill_chunker.py (line 463). This is the 619-line section-aware XML-smart chunker that parses <section>/<subsection>/<paragraph>/<quoted-block> tags with three-tier strategy (preamble → section_split → subsection_split → text_split_fallback) and a regex fallback for non-XML bills.

The right fix: congress_chunks should route bill-typed documents through chunk_bill_text instead of falling through to generic char-count splitting. Same pattern as media-ingest's recent unification — one chunker entry point, domain-aware dispatch.

Concrete plan:
- assets/chunks.py: when doc.document_type == 'bill' and doc.metadata has bill XML, dispatch to chunk_bill_text. Otherwise use the existing generic + passthrough routing.
- Keep bill_tail.py wired to chunk_bill_text for backward compat (it produces the document-first benchmark fixtures).
- Verify benchmark_chunks.json doesn't regenerate to lose XML structure when congress_chunks runs.
- Optionally: extract chunk_bill_text into ChunkingResource.chunk_bill_xml(...) so the bill chunker becomes a sibling method like chunk_speaker_segments — keeps the 'one Chunker resource, multiple strategies' architecture clean.

Blocking risk: bill_chunker has its own ChunkConfig dependency (libs/dagster-io/src/dagster_io/chunking.py) and may need re-fitting to take a ChunkingResource for prepend_title/CHUNK_SIZE/CHUNK_OVERLAP consistency.
acceptance_criteria: congress_chunks asset produces section-aware chunks for bill documents (chunks have section/subsection metadata, not just chunk_size-bounded splits). Non-bill document types (member_profile, committee_profile) keep their existing routing. Benchmark fixtures regenerated and inspected to confirm XML structure is preserved. Other congress doc types unaffected.
notes:
ADDITIONAL FINDING (2026-05-01):

The benchmark fixtures `tests/fixtures/congress-data/benchmark_documents.json` (3 bills) are stored as plain text — no XML markup. Confirmed via inspection. metadata has 'has_xml' flag set but the `text` field is text-extracted prose.

Result: bill_chunker.py's XML mode never fires for benchmark scoring. All 4 chunks in the current benchmark_chunks.json have `parse_mode: "regex"` — the chunker tried XML, found none, fell back to plain-text regex matching on "SECTION X." / "Sec. N." headings. The XML structural-parsing code path is effectively dead for benchmarks.

This means:
- Benchmark scoring tests regex-fallback chunking, not the XML chunker that production runs on real Congress.gov XML
- Strategy labeling is also misleading — `strategy: "section_split"` looks the same in both XML and regex mode; only `parse_mode` distinguishes

Two follow-ups that should land alongside the original wire-up:

1. LABELING: Differentiate strategy names in bill_chunker — `xml_section_split` vs `regex_section_split` (and `xml_subsection_split` vs `regex_subsection_split`). UI can then surface "structural parsing happened" at a glance without reading parse_mode.

2. FIXTURE REALISM: Re-generate benchmark_documents.json to preserve raw bill XML. Either:
   - Store XML in the existing `text` field (chunker auto-detects via XML tags), OR
   - Add `metadata.bill_xml` and update bill_chunker to prefer that field
   This is needed before XML-chunker quality can be benchmarked at all.

LocalJsonIOManager promoted to dagster_io with Optional/Append variants, select_io_managers backend selector, task dev runs all 3 code locations against local FS, per-domain integration tests + Taskfile targets, multi-shape load_chunks() with sample_per_domain cap, scripts/regen_benchmark_chunks.py deleted, _tests/ deleted, docs updated (TESTING/BENCHMARK/README + 2 blogs + CHUNKING). Verified: 3 domains materialized, dagster UI loads all 3, Playwright smoke passed. CD-1pfd: bill_chunker now handles both <legis-body> and <resolution-body>, regression-tested.

title: LangGraph ai_context node — chunk-level summary attached to each mention
description:
Add a new LangGraph node 'ai_context' to the validated extraction pipeline that produces a one-sentence chunk-level summary of what's being discussed, attached to every Mention in the chunk via a new Mention.ai_context field (or Provenance.context_summary). One LLM call per chunk amortized across all mentions in that chunk.

Pipeline placement (after repair, before SPO):
    chunk → NER → validate → repair → ai_context → SPO

Why: today's Mention.context is a raw character window from chunk.text (just shipped — extraction.py:380-388). It's brittle (mid-sentence cuts, off-topic words) and not useful for embedding-based retrieval, dedup, or human inspection in the UI side panel. An AI summary captures *what was happening* not just *nearby words*.

Architecture decisions:

1. PER-CHUNK BATCHED, NOT PER-MENTION. Per-mention would mean 100-500x extra LLM calls per chunk — explosive cost. Per-chunk: one LLM call returns one summary, every mention in that chunk shares it. Tractable: ~1 extra call per chunk per model.

2. TIER 2 ONLY FOR V1. The 'progressive summarization' hierarchy has 4 tiers (mention-context / chunk-summary / section-summary / document-summary). Start with Tier 2 (chunk-summary) — cheapest with highest leverage. Tier 1 (per-mention sentence summary) defer until usage data justifies it. Tiers 3-4 (composed across chunks) are future work.

3. ENV-GATED. AI_CONTEXT_ENABLED=true to opt in. Default off. Latency cost: +1 LLM call per chunk per model. For 7 videos × ~500 chunks × 12 models that's 42K extra calls. Need either a fast cheap summarizer (gpt-4o-mini, claude-haiku) or run only when comparing models on small-N chunks.

4. SCHEMA. Add Mention.ai_context: str = '' (or extend Provenance with context_summary: str). Update extraction_schemas.py + extraction.py:372 (mention construction) + viewer-ui benchmark types + viewer SPA panel that displays it.

Implementation phases:

Phase 1 (~50 lines): AIContextNode class in catalyst-langgraph-aio with chunk-summary prompt. Add to graph after repair. Returns same GraphState with summary attached to each mention dict.

Phase 2 (~30 lines): Plumb through extract_validated() to populate Mention.ai_context. Update Mention pydantic model. Update extraction output JSON.

Phase 3 (~20 lines): Viewer SPA side panel renders ai_context alongside raw context.

Phase 4 (deferred): Tier 1 (per-mention sentence summaries via batched per-chunk call) once usage data justifies the latency.

Phase 5 (deferred): Tier 3-4 (section + document summaries via composition).
acceptance_criteria: With AI_CONTEXT_ENABLED=true: every mention in a fresh extraction has mention.ai_context populated with a one-sentence chunk-level summary. Default off (AI_CONTEXT_ENABLED unset): zero behavior change, no extra LLM calls. Viewer SPA side panel displays ai_context when present, gracefully omits when empty. Benchmark harness reports the AI context cost alongside extraction cost in stats.
notes:
Cost is the dominant constraint. A small fast summarizer (~250 tok/s) on a 53-chunk video adds ~10-30s per model. On 7 videos × ~500 chunks × 12 models the math gets ugly fast — need either:
- a SUMMARIZER_MODEL env var that's cheap regardless of which extraction model is being benchmarked (single fast model for all summary calls)
- or run with --no-ai-context flag for full panel benchmarks; only enable for single-model deep-dive runs

Don't replace the raw text-window context already in extraction.py:380-388. Keep both — UI consumers can show raw window for debugging, ai_context for human inspection. Embedding consumers prefer ai_context.

Ties into:
- CD-uu76 (embedding-derived chunking) — ai_context summaries could BE the embeddings used for similarity-based chunk merging.
- CD-vfiq (multi-video GT/scoring) — per-mention context summaries make cross-video dedup easier.
- The viewer-SPA entity side panel currently being built — this is the natural slot for displaying ai_context.

title: Multi-video ensemble GT + scoring across audio_manifest
description:
Wire ensemble ground-truth generation and F1 scoring to operate per-video across the audio_manifest.yaml so multi-video benchmark runs (--all-videos) produce comparable scoring data per (model, video) pair, not just aggregate counts.

Current state after multi-video extraction work:
- benchmark_harness.py --all-videos invokes scripts/bench_extract_per_video.py per model
- Per-video extraction artifacts land at runs/<run-id>/extractions/<doc_id>/extraction_<model>.json
- Aggregate (video-roll-up) extraction artifact at runs/<run-id>/extractions/extraction_<model>.json (mentions/assertions empty by design — per-video files are source of truth)
- BenchmarkStore + RunStore extended with optional doc_id arg for per-video lookups

What's missing:
1. _run_ensemble_gt: today builds GT from a single set of per-model extractions. Needs to iterate manifest doc_ids and build a per-video GT dict. Save shape: ground-truth/<doc_id>/active.json (mirroring extractions/<doc_id>/ layout) OR a single ground-truth/active.json keyed by doc_id internally.
2. _score_latest / compute_model_scores: today expects a single chunks_data + GT. For multi-video runs, score per (model, video), aggregate to per-model F1 weighted by chunk count.
3. report builder (build_report_json): today produces a flat per-model report. Needs per-video breakdown (table: rows=models, cols=videos × {strict_f1, span_f1, mention_count}) + per-model rollup.
4. Viewer SPA: extra column/tab for video selection.

Implementation phases:
A. Per-video GT save/load API on BenchmarkStore (1-2 hours).
B. _run_ensemble_gt iterates manifest, builds per-video GT, saves with doc_id (2-3 hours).
C. _score_latest iterates per (model, doc_id) extractions, computes per-pair F1, aggregates (2-3 hours).
D. report.build_report_json adds 'per_video' section with per-pair stats (1-2 hours).
E. Viewer SPA gets video selector (2-4 hours, frontend work).

Phase A-D unblocks multi-video CLI scoring without UI work; E is polish.
acceptance_criteria: task bench --all-videos --models gliner-medium followed by task bench:report shows per-(model, video) F1 + per-model aggregates across the 7 manifest videos. Existing single-video --models flow remains unchanged for back-compat. Viewer SPA shows video selector picking which video's per-model breakdown to display.
notes:
Open questions: how to weight per-video F1 in the per-model rollup (chunk-weighted vs equal-per-video)? Should aggregate F1 be macro (avg of per-video) or micro (concat then F1)? Current single-video uses micro. Default to micro for back-compat; expose macro as a flag.

GT generation cost: ensemble GT today runs ~30 min wall clock on a single video. Per-video on 7 videos = ~3.5 hours. Acceptable as a one-time setup; users won't regen often.

Not blocking: today's --all-videos run produces extraction artifacts that can be inspected manually even without per-video scoring. Scoring is the F1 layer on top of extraction data.

Children of CD-6ef7 epic indirectly (chunking strategy work feeds into per-video extraction quality).

title: [epic] Advanced per-domain chunking via LangChain splitters + EmbeddingResource integration
description:
Pull in LangChain's chunking-strategy zoo, wrap each as a method on ChunkingResource so the API stays unified, and integrate EmbeddingResource for semantic strategies. Each of the 3 domains gets the optimal strategy for its content type instead of the current one-size-fits-all RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter for text + custom speaker chunker for audio.

Per-domain target strategies:
- media-ingest: chunk_speaker_segments (current, keep) + chunk_semantic refinement layer (CD-uu76)
- congress-data: MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter for bill structure (sections/subsections); section-aware bill_chunker.py already exists, formalize it as a ChunkingResource method
- open-leaks: SemanticChunker for cables (short topical units), HTMLHeaderTextSplitter or section-aware for court documents
- all domains: TokenTextSplitter (tiktoken) as a token-budget-aware option for LLM context fitting (replaces guessing at char counts)

Integration architecture:
- ChunkingResource gains LangChain-wrapper methods alongside existing ones. Each returns list[TextChunk] with same provenance fields (chunk_id, content_hash, start_s/end_s where applicable).
- For semantic strategies, take EmbeddingResource as a runtime arg (not constructor dep) — chunker doesn't import OpenAI/HuggingFace, just consumes whatever embedder produces. Add EmbeddingResource.langchain_embedder() accessor returning the underlying langchain.Embeddings object.
- Per-domain chunks.py asset picks the right method based on doc.document_type (already has the routing pattern in congress + leaks).

Phases:
1. Inventory: list LangChain splitters in current langchain-text-splitters version, map to domain types, document tradeoffs.
2. ChunkingResource API extension: add chunk_semantic, chunk_markdown_headers, chunk_by_tokens, refine_with_semantic. Each is a thin wrapper around LangChain that converts output to TextChunk.
3. Per-domain wiring: update congress_chunks asset to use chunk_markdown_headers for bills; leak_chunks to use chunk_semantic for cables; media_chunks gets refine_with_semantic as opt-in (CD-uu76).
4. Benchmark comparison: run extraction harness with each new strategy, record F1 delta vs baseline.
5. Documentation: update CHUNKING.md docs in each domain + the shared dagster_io/chunking.py docstring with the new strategy menu.
acceptance_criteria: ChunkingResource exposes 3+ new LangChain-wrapped methods (chunk_semantic, chunk_markdown_headers, chunk_by_tokens). EmbeddingResource has a langchain_embedder() accessor. Each domain's chunks.py asset is updated to use the optimal strategy for its primary document type. Benchmark F1 delta documented.
notes:
ARCHITECTURE DECISION: per-subtype chunks assets, factory-generated, with thin collector downstream. NOT a single asset with by_type dict config.

Rationale: each subtype asset has its own simple flat ChunkConfig (no dict editor in launchpad), strategy is encoded in asset identity (congress_bill_chunks IS the bill chunker), downstream extraction is unchanged (collector concatenates).

Pattern (per code location):

    # factory eliminates boilerplate
    def _chunks_asset(name, doc_type, default_strategy, **defaults): ...

    congress_bill_chunks      = _chunks_asset("congress_bill_chunks", "bill", "markdown_headers", chunk_size=4000)
    congress_member_chunks    = _chunks_asset("congress_member_chunks", "member_profile", "passthrough")
    congress_committee_chunks = _chunks_asset("congress_committee_chunks", "committee_profile", "passthrough")

    @asset
    def congress_chunks(bill_chunks, member_chunks, committee_chunks) -> list[TextChunk]:
        return [*bill_chunks, *member_chunks, *committee_chunks]   # thin collector

Wins:
- Each asset's ChunkConfig is flat (strategy + a few knobs) — clean launchpad UI per asset
- Asset graph encodes the routing visually (bills → bill_chunks; members → member_chunks)
- Independent re-materialization per subtype
- Adding a new subtype is one factory line
- Downstream mentions/assertions/embeddings unchanged (they take the collector)

Per-domain map:
- congress: bill (markdown_headers), member (passthrough), committee (passthrough) → congress_chunks collector
- open-leaks: cable (semantic), court_document (markdown_headers), offshore_entity (passthrough) → leak_chunks collector
- media-ingest: media_chunks (speaker_turn) — single subtype today; collector added when variants emerge

Replaces the previous "Pattern A vs B (single strategy per run vs by_type dict)" decision. Hybrid via per-subtype assets is strictly better: no UI dict editor + per-subtype lineage in Dagster + per-asset config simplicity.

title: Embedding-derived chunking strategy — POC + benchmark eval
description:
Add semantic-similarity-driven chunking as a new ChunkingResource strategy alongside chunk_speaker_segments / chunk_document. Use embeddings between adjacent segments to detect topic-shift boundaries instead of (or layered on) mechanical thresholds (max_chars, pause_threshold_s).

Three plausible architectures:
A. Standalone strategy — chunking.chunk_semantic_boundary(segments, embeddings, doc_id, title). Pure semantic; ignores speaker. Best for text-heavy domains (congress, leaks).
B. Post-pass refinement — chunking.refine_with_semantic(chunks, embedder). Takes chunk_speaker_segments output; merges adjacent same-speaker chunks with high cosine similarity, splits oversize chunks at internal similarity dips. Preserves speaker-aware machinery; layered hybrid.
C. Replace tier 2 (speech_pause_split) — split oversize turns at lowest-similarity sentence boundary instead of 1.0s word gap.

Recommended: option B (post-pass refinement). Preserves speaker provenance (chunk_id, content_hash, start_s/end_s, speaker metadata) which downstream extraction depends on. Adds topic awareness as an opt-in overlay behind a feature flag (SEMANTIC_REFINE_CHUNKS=true).

Implementation phases:
1. Histogram POC (~30 lines, ~2h): on existing chunks from a benchmark run, embed with sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 — fast), log adjacent-chunk cosine similarity distribution. Pure observation, no behavior change. Provides empirical data on whether semantic boundaries even matter for current content.
2. If signal present: implement chunking.refine_with_semantic(chunks, embedder, merge_threshold=0.85, split_threshold=0.4). Percentile-based thresholds preferred over absolute (LangChain SemanticChunker style). ~1 day.
3. Compare via benchmark harness — run with refinement on/off across same model panel; record F1 delta on mention extraction. Use existing 'bench --compare' mode. ~1 day.
4. Production: Dagster asset, OTEL metrics (semantic_merge_count, semantic_split_count), CHUNKING.md docs, threshold tuning notebook.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 1 (histogram POC) committed and ran against existing pipeline-cache; histogram saved as artifact. Decision documented (proceed/abandon) based on observed signal. If proceed: phase 2-3 produce a feature-flagged opt-in path with measurable F1 delta on the benchmark harness.
notes:
Architectural complication: today embeddings happen DOWNSTREAM of chunks (media_chunks → media_embeddings). Embedding-derived chunking inverts the dependency — chunker needs segment-level embeddings. Two ways out: (a) two-pass embeddings (segments first cheap, then chunks like today), or (b) move embeddings upstream and have downstream embedding be averaging.

Provenance must be preserved: chunk_id, content_hash, asset lineage from media_chunks → media_mentions/media_assertions/media_embeddings is load-bearing.

Don't replace chunk_speaker_segments — speaker boundaries are needed for diarization-aware extraction (mentions tied to specific speakers). Refinement-as-overlay is the right shape.

title: LangGraph nodes as Dagster op steps for fine-grained observability
description: Currently extract_validated() runs the entire LangGraph pipeline (chunk→NER→validate→repair→SPO→persist) as a single Dagster op step. The Dagster UI shows one black box. Goal: expose individual LangGraph nodes (extract_ner, validate_ner, repair_ner, extract_spo, etc.) as Dagster op steps so each node appears in the run timeline with its own duration, status, and metadata. This gives Dagit-level observability into the extraction pipeline without breaking the LangGraph graph topology. Approach: use Dagster's @graph_asset or @op composition to wrap LangGraph node execution. Each LangGraph node emits an AssetObservation or op event. LangGraph still owns the conditional edges (validate→repair loop), but Dagster sees each step. Must preserve: SDA lineage (chunks→mentions→assertions), partition support, OTEL metrics, audit event trail.
design: Option A: @graph_asset that decomposes extract_validated into individual @ops (extract_ner_op, validate_ner_op, etc.) wired with Dagster graph edges. LangGraph nodes become thin wrappers called by Dagster ops. Option B: Keep LangGraph as execution engine but emit Dagster AssetObservation events from each node via a callback/hook. Dagster sees the timeline without controlling the topology. Option B is simpler and preserves LangGraph's conditional edge logic (repair loops). Recommend B.

title: Ground Truth Review & Edit UI in Benchmark Viewer
description:

2. **Review panel** — side panel or modal showing current ground truth data per chunk: mentions with types/spans, propositions with S-P-O
3. **Edit ability** — inline editing of ground truth: add/remove/modify mentions and propositions, fix entity types, correct spans
4. **Save** — write changes back to ground truth JSON, set `manually_reviewed: true`
5. **Re-score** — button to trigger re-scoring all models against updated ground truth

Ground truth lives at `.test-output/media-ingest/fixtures/ground_truth_media_ingest.json`.
The viewer SPA is at `packages/media-ingest/viewer-ui/`.
Format: `{ chunks: [{ chunk_id, text, mentions: [{text, mention_type, span_start, span_end, confidence}], propositions: [{subject, predicate, object, confidence}] }] }`

1. Ground truth tab appears in benchmark page tab bar
2. Loads and displays ground_truth_media_ingest.json (chunk list with mentions/propositions)
3. User can select which ground truth file to view (if multiple exist)
4. Inline editing: add/remove/modify mentions (text, type, span) and propositions (S-P-O)
